articles.title: The UAE embraces AI for kindergartners
articles.summary:
In September, Henry Price observed a classroom of 7- to 8-year-olds learn about the Stone Age. They discussed and wrote about cave paintings, then put on virtual reality headsets to explore them.
The founding principal of Rugby School Dubai hopes his students will soon study ancient Egypt the same way — reading about it, creating artwork, and then stepping inside a virtual pyramid, or using artificial intelligence to “interview” a pharaoh.
“AI does not replace reading, writing, discussion, or creativity. It enhances them and opens new doors,” Price told Rest of World. “We want our students to be excited by AI, but never [be] passive users. We want children who use AI to ask better questions, not children who rely on it to give them all the answers.”
The United Arab Emirates recently became the first country to make AI a required K-12 subject.
That puts the country on one side of a growing global debate over what children should learn about AI and when they should encounter it. While the UAE and China are treating early AI literacy as a national priority, some Western governments are moving in the opposite direction. New York City introduced a one-year moratorium on student-facing generative AI in public schools from preschool through grade eight, citing concerns about children’s mental health. Norway has also enacted a similar near-ban for primary school children.

articles.title: Introducing Firefox Enterprise | The Mozilla Blog
articles.summary:
Mozilla introduces Firefox Enterprise
Institutions are recalculating who controls the technology they rely on. Mozilla has an independent option to offer.
For years, organizations consolidated technology around a small number of providers to make things simpler. Fewer systems. Tighter integrations. More economies of scale. But that consolidation went well beyond technology. It consolidated dependency, too. The resulting risks have been debated, studied, and challenged along the way, but concentration continued. More work, data and critical infrastructure kept moving to the same few providers, while credible alternatives narrowed.
The deeper that dependency runs, the harder and more costly it becomes to change course. When something fails, changes or falls outside an institution’s control, that dependency becomes a risk for CIOs and CISOs to manage.
Nowhere are these stakes more visible than in Europe. Now institutions are re-assessing. Governments are pushing for greater digital autonomy, while regulated industries face growing pressure to find and manage their dependencies.
There’s a name for much of this debate about technological control: “sovereignty.”
What digital sovereignty means in practice varies. Across Europe, governments are investing in the security and resilience of critical IT infrastructure, reducing strategic dependencies and putting technological autonomy higher on national agendas. Different approaches, same underlying concern. Strip away the regional polic…

articles.title: Claude : après une nouvelle dérive, Anthropic prive certaines IA d'accès Internet
articles.summary:
Depuis juillet, Anthropic épluche les journaux de ses campagnes de test, ces sessions où ses modèles répètent des centaines, parfois des milliers de fois la même tâche pour mesurer leurs progrès. Le bilan publié le 9 octobre recense quatre familles de dérapages commis sur de vrais sites web, dont certains appartiennent à des administrations américaines. Une sanction accompagne le rapport : plus aucune évaluation interne n’aura accès à Internet tant que les outils de surveillance du laboratoire n’auront pas fait leurs preuves.
Un faux tuyau pour un vrai meurtre
Le 18 juillet vers 23 h 30, le formulaire de PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, le site de la police de Philadelphie consacré aux meurtres non élucidés, reçoit ce message : « j’ai peut-être des informations sur cette affaire. Je me souviens avoir vu quelqu’un correspondant à la description dans le secteur à cette période. » L’auteur s’appelle Claude Haiku 4.5. Chargé de générer des interactions d’exemple sur des pages web tirées au hasard, le modèle est tombé sur l’affaire, a rempli le champ libre, laissé vides le nom et le contact, puis validé. La page ne contenait aucune description du suspect ; classé comme spam, le message n’a jamais atteint les enquêteurs.
La police n’a appris son existence que le 7 octobre, alors qu’Anthropic avait repéré l’incident fin septembre. Le département juge ce délai « inacceptable », tout en confirmant qu’aucun de ses systèmes n’a été compromis.

articles.title: Facebook vai deixar você personalizar o algoritmo do feed com IA
articles.summary:
O Facebook está lançando o Your Algorithm (“Seu Algoritmo”), recurso que permite aos usuários indicar quais assuntos desejam ver com mais ou menos frequência no Feed e nos Reels. A ferramenta usa inteligência artificial (IA) para ajustar as recomendações a partir dessas preferências.
A novidade amplia as formas de interação com o algoritmo da rede social: em vez de depender apenas das curtidas, dos comentários e dos vídeos assistidos para identificar interesses, o sistema também poderá receber instruções escritas pelos próprios usuários.
Como personalizar o feed
O recurso, lançado anteriormente no Instagram, permite adicionar e gerenciar temas de interesse em um espaço dedicado, acessível pelo menu de três pontos das publicações.
Nesse mesmo menu, será possível marcar as opções “Tenho interesse” ou “Não tenho interesse”. Os botões também poderão aparecer diretamente abaixo de algumas publicações. Dependendo da resposta, o Facebook poderá fazer perguntas adicionais para entender melhor a preferência do usuário.
Outra possibilidade é explicar em palavras próprias o que se deseja encontrar com mais ou menos frequência. Segundo a Meta, as recomendações serão atualizadas em tempo real, com ajustes que podem ocorrer durante a própria sessão de uso.

articles.title: ¿Cuánta IA hay en los libros más vendidos? Mucha en novelas románticas de Amazon y en el superventas de Alvise Pérez
articles.summary:
¿Cuánta IA hay en los libros más vendidos? Mucha en novelas románticas de Amazon y en el superventas de Alvise Pérez
EL PAÍS ha analizado 175 libros populares con el detector Pangram. En 2019 no hay ni rastro, pero ahora uno de cada tres superventas autopublicados está escrito en su mayor parte con inteligencia artificial
La inteligencia artificial llega también al mundo de los libros. EL PAÍS ha comprobado el uso de IA en una muestra concreta de 119 libros populares de 2025 y 2026: hemos analizado los volúmenes aparecidos en las listas de superventas en Amazon y la Casa del Libro, y en los ganadores de un gran premio literario.
Todos los libros con un uso mayoritario de IA que ha encontrado este periódico han sido autopublicados, muchos de ellos en la categoría de novelas románticas. Son libros con numerosos lectores: tienen entre 270 y 2.000 valoraciones en Amazon.
El caso más visible es Devuélveme mi país, del político Alvise Pérez. En febrero de 2026 fue número 1 en Amazon. Pangram clasifica como generado por IA el 97% de todo el libro; ese porcentaje es la parte del libro que atribuye a una máquina. Es decir, que casi todo el texto saldría de un programa como ChatGPT o similares y solo un 3% sería solo humano, según la herramienta, que no dice quién usó la IA ni cómo lo hizo. No aclara si le pidieron el texto completo o si le dio sus notas o ideas para que las ampliara. articles.title: Should Carney give Canadian tech a (tax) break?
articles.summary:
Two years ago, Canada’s then-governing Liberal Party proposed a capital gains tax inclusion rate hike, and much of the country’s tech sector freaked out. While this plan was scrapped after Mark Carney replaced Justin Trudeau as party leader, the surprise decision and the message it conveyed had severely hurt the Liberals’ relationship with Canadian tech. As Roadmunk co-founder Latif Nanji told me last year, “The damage [was] done.”
Today, many of the same industry leaders have penned an open letter asking Carney’s Liberals for a capital gains rollover and a US QSBS-style tax incentive in the upcoming federal budget to better retain Canada’s entrepreneurs, talent, and capital. The key difference this time around is that both parties seem more receptive to working together.
As NACO CEO Claudio Rojas told BetaKit, “We want to see Canadian companies succeed, we want to control our own destiny, and that aligns quite well with the signals that we’re seeing from this government that they’re willing to take action.”
Hundreds of Canadian CEOs, investors, and other business leaders have signed the open letter. Its authors frame these measures as a means of derisking investments in domestic firms and incentivizing the reinvestment of associated profits in Canada.

Google makes it easier to launch your vibe-coded apps
You can now launch your vibe-coded app directly from the Google Play Store.
Google first launched the ability to vibe-code personal Android apps in May. Even though you can now launch your custom apps in Google Play, the company notes it will continue to keep them “secure, private, and separate from the public store catalog.” You can also launch them using a standard Google account, and the company will soon add the ability to share your app with a select group of people, too.
Though this might make it easier to play around with experimental apps, Google is positioning it as an on-ramp of sorts for fledgling developers. “If you want to share your app with the world, Google Play helps you graduate to a professional developer account with the same Trust & Safety reviews and high-quality standards as professional developers,” Sam Bright, Google’s vice president and general manager of Google Play, writes in the announcement.

articles.title: Windows 10 : à partir de juin 2027, ces PC ne recevront plus rien, absolument plus rien, de Windows Update
articles.summary:
Windows 10 : à partir de juin 2027, ces PC ne recevront plus rien, absolument plus rien, de Windows Update
Privés de correctifs de sécurité depuis octobre 2025, les PC restés sous Windows 10 sans le programme de sécurité étendue (ESU) gardent encore un fil avec Microsoft. Le 19 juin 2027, il cassera net, et la porte de sortie, pourtant gratuite en France, pourrait se refermer plus tôt qu'annoncé.
Depuis la fin du support de Windows 10, le 14 octobre 2025, un PC non inscrit aux mises à jour de sécurité étendues (ESU) ne reçoit plus le moindre correctif pour Windows. Il reste pourtant branché sur Windows Update. Par ce canal transitent notamment les définitions de l'antivirus Microsoft Defender, que l'éditeur s'est engagé à fournir sur Windows 10 jusqu'en octobre 2028. Ce dernier lien a désormais une date de fin. Dans une note publiée le 8 octobre, Microsoft explique que les certificats permettant aux PC de vérifier qu'ils dialoguent avec ses véritables serveurs expirent les 17 mai et 19 juin 2027. Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down
More than 20% of the web sits behind Cloudflare’s network, and our team, the Data team, owns the data pipeline responsible for plumbing that data (and more) from our global network to applicable central data centers. The Cloudflare network is a globally distributed system supporting tens of thousands of servers. Data that power Cloudflare Logs, SQL API, observability, internal analytics, and more flow through this network and use our data pipeline to serve customers.
In May of this year, we were providing data delivery at roughly two billion events per second. This includes customer traffic as well as data sent from internal teams. Year after year, we tackle the same problem — exponential traffic growth against linear hardware growth. We have to react to this increase in order to keep resource costs under control. Over the past five years, we’ve made various improvements to compensate for the data volume increase in comparison to hardware allocation, equivalent to deferring two and a half years of hardware expansion. This post details those changes: breaking up our monolithic data schema in 2022, adjusting compression in 2024, rearchitecting pipeline replication in spring 2026, decentralizing sampling in summer 2026, and introducing aggregations into the pipeline in fall 2026.

Pour faire simple, le DLSS fait un rendu des images successives du jeu en basse définition (1080p par exemple) et se sert de l’IA pour reconstruire l’image dans la définition de l’écran (1440p, 4K ou autres). En interne, le jeu calcule donc ses images dans une définition inférieure, ce qui soulage la carte graphique et fait grimper les performances.
Le mode Performance dont il est question ici concerne une autre brique du DLSS, la génération d’images (Frame Generation). Le jeu calcule de vraies images, et l’IA en intercale d’autres entre deux d’entre elles, en s’appuyant sur des données fournies par le jeu, comme les vecteurs de mouvement et la profondeur, pour comprendre comment les objets se déplacent d’une image à l’autre.
L’un des résultats les plus concrets est la hausse du nombre d’images par seconde. Nvidia veut justement la pousser encore plus loin avec une mise à jour du DLSS 5, annoncée ce mardi 13 octobre. Artificial Intelligence
Mixture-of-Experts kernel engineering on Amazon SageMaker AI
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a sparsely-activated architecture that scales large language model (LLM) capacity while keeping per-token compute low. Because its operations account for a large share of total compute time, inefficiencies there directly raise request latency and cost. Therefore, optimizing MoE operations through kernel engineering offers the largest opportunity for performance gains.
Fused MoE is a key optimization technique for the MoE architecture. A fused MoE system merges token routing, data shuffling, and specialized network calculations into a single batched operation on the GPU. This replaces executing those routing and expert computations as separate, sequential loop operations. While this provides latency advantages, it also brings complexity in kernel implementations and debugging capability. High GPU utilization for this architecture requires hardware-specific optimizations.
In this post, we describe the different kernel optimizations we implemented for fused MoE models and show you how you can benefit from this work. We used a representative MoE model as our primary example.

articles.title: What’s old is new: Lightwell discovers novel zero-day vulnerability in core Java framework
articles.summary:
Enterprise IT runs on decades-old foundational code. The prevailing assumption around these mature components is that if code has been sitting untouched in production for ten years without breaking, it must be safe. Libraries like the Eclipse Implementation of Jakarta XML Binding (JAXB) quietly power enterprise applications in the background. Embedded deep into middleware stacks and application servers, they carry heavy workloads without drawing attention.
Advanced AI security tooling doesn’t ignore these deep-stack layers, however. It finds zero-day flaws hidden in structural parsing logic that standard static analysis tools miss entirely. And discovery is only part of the story. Any new vulnerabilities impacting these load-bearing pillars need to be discovered, analyzed, and swiftly addressed by the community. This is exactly what Lightwell did with a novel vulnerability within JAXB, identified as CVE-2026-92877.
Addressing novel flaws across the software lifecycle
When a vulnerability is discovered in a new framework, communities and maintainers respond quickly. The code is fresh, developers are actively tweaking it, and patches roll out quickly. Legacy components face a different reality. Unaddressed flaws in fundamental XML binding logic can compromise every application server, middleware pipeline, and cloud service that relies on it.

articles.title: India delays digital payments fee rollout amid retailer pushback | TechCrunch

Following broad pushback from merchants across the country, India has delayed plans to introduce merchant fees on its digital payments network that aimed to make the business more lucrative for the companies that facilitate the payments service, long dominated by Google and PhonePe.
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), which operates the country’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI), said on Tuesday it was postponing the planned October 15 rollout of a 0.4% fee on eligible merchant transactions exceeding ₹2,000 (about $21), citing the festive shopping season. The fee, announced last month, would mark a significant departure from India’s years-long policy of keeping UPI payments free for merchants.
The rollout will now take place after Diwali, one of India’s biggest festivals and shopping periods, though the NPCI did not specify a new date. In September alone, UPI processed 24.07 billion transactions worth ₹29.37 trillion (about $305 billion), per NPCI.
The proposed fee drew opposition from retailers and petrol pump operators, some of whom warned they could stop accepting UPI payments if the charge took effect.
Over the past several years, UPI has become the backbone of India’s digital payments system, powering payments through apps such as Google Pay, PhonePe, and Paytm. Its growth has been supported by the Indian government keeping UPI payments free for merchants and providing subsidies to banks and payment providers to help them cover some of the costs.

articles.title: Multa de R$ 138 milhões faz Meta acionar Suprema Corte em Londres
articles.summary:
A Meta, dona do Facebook e do Instagram, contestou na Justiça britânica os critérios usados pelo regulador de mídia Ofcom para calcular taxas e multas previstas na Lei de Segurança Online. A empresa considera desproporcional o uso da receita mundial como base para essas cobranças.
O processo começou nesta terça-feira (13), na Alta Corte de Londres, uma semana depois de o órgão abrir uma investigação para apurar se a Meta avaliou adequadamente os riscos do recurso Instagram Instants antes de lançá-lo, em maio.
O que está em jogo no cálculo das multas
Aprovada em 2023, a Lei de Segurança Online permite que o Ofcom aplique multas de até 10% da receita mundial qualificável de uma empresa ou 18 milhões de libras (cerca de R$ 120 milhões), prevalecendo o valor maior. A legislação também autoriza o órgão a cobrar taxas para cobrir os custos de fiscalização, calculadas com base na receita.
A Meta argumenta que o regulador extrapolou os poderes previstos na lei ao adotar uma definição ampla de receita mundial qualificável. Na contestação, a empresa afirma que o método abre caminho para as maiores penalidades possíveis. Também questiona como são calculadas as multas quando duas ou mais empresas do mesmo grupo são consideradas conjuntamente responsáveis por uma infração.
O Ofcom defende sua metodologia. Segundo o órgão, a receita mundial serve apenas para determinar o limite máximo de uma eventual penalidade; a multa efetiva deve ser proporcional à infração.

articles.title: Cyberattack Prompts Grocery Giant Ahold Delhaize to Disconnect Systems
articles.summary:
Dutch-Belgian grocery giant Ahold Delhaize has disconnected some of its systems in response to a cyberattack.
In a bare-bones notice on its website, the company revealed that it identified a security issue within its network, triggering incident response.
“Our teams are taking steps to assess and mitigate the issue. This includes taking some systems offline to help protect them,” the company said.
Ahold Delhaize said its stores remain open and that its ability to serve customers has not been affected.
According to local media, the preventive measures impacted deliveries and online orders at Albert Heijn and Delhaize brands in Belgium and the Netherlands. Stores in the US appear to have been affected as well.
In a Tuesday update, the company confirmed that its brands’ stores are experiencing issues.
“The impact of our preventative measures differs per brand. Each local brand is working hard to serve its customers and minimize disruption,” Ahold Delhaize said.
It also noted that its security team is getting ready to restore the affected systems, but did not provide an estimated timeline.
“Our teams are working with urgency to investigate the incident and restore affected systems safely. As they make progress in assessing and mitigating the issues, we are in the process of starting a controlled re-launch of certain systems,” the company said.

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary:
Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: If AI prompts can build your product, will African VCs still invest?
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped how the world works, and African AI startups, venture capital and tech ecosystems are no exception. The technology is evolving so fast that many investors are still working out how to evaluate AI startups, let alone how to fund them. Over the past six months, this column has spoken to African investors across regions, sectors, and funding stages about where AI creates genuine value, where it falls short, and what merits institutional capital. They are Babacar Seck , founder of Askya Investment Partners; Eloho Omame , partner at TLcom Capital; Emmanuel Adegboye , head of Madica; Magnifique Ishimwe , fund manager at the Development Bank of Rwanda; Husein Merchant , investment officer at Village Capital; and Benjamin Toulouze, head of corporate venture capital at AXIAN Investment. When we asked them what makes an AI startup fundable, they mostly described something an AI model itself cannot supply. Anyone can build on the same foundational models now, so investors are paying for what sits around them: voice products that work in Wolof and isiZulu, software tied so deeply into a customer’s systems that leaving is painful, licences that take years to win, and revenue. Voice is where they see the clearest opening. Adegboye says the opportunity lies in building on top of foundational models with local data, and above all in voice. C’est un phénomène classique : la connexion est impeccable dans le salon, mais le signal faiblit dans la chambre des enfants, voire disparaît dans le bureau au fond du couloir. articles.title: Anthropic cree que algunos de sus modelos pequeños ya tienen la capacidad de propagarse sin intervención humana
articles.summary:
William Zhou y Daniel Freeman, dos investigadores de Anthropic, han publicado en la página web de este laboratorio un artículo que con toda seguridad va a desencadenar un debate intenso. El título de su texto es muy revelador: "Los modelos de IA pueden ser capaces de autorreplicarse sin acceder a un centro de datos". Es un titular muy directo que nos invita a hacernos una pregunta evidente: si los modelos de inteligencia artificial (IA) no necesitan acceder a un centro de datos, ¿dónde podrían autorreplicarse?
Según Zhou y Freeman, algunos modelos pequeños podrían adquirir en pocos meses la capacidad de propagarse sin intervención humana utilizando el hardware de algunos dispositivos de consumo que muchos de nosotros tenemos en casa, como los televisores, los electrodomésticos u otros aparatos dotados de conexión a internet y un SoC mínimamente capaz. Suena a ciencia ficción, pero no lo es. Los dos investigadores de Anthropic aseguran que han llegado a esta conclusión después de llevar a cabo experimentos que exploran cómo estos sistemas podrían propagarse sin intervención humana.
En su artículo plantean un escenario en el que un modelo de IA lo suficientemente avanzado podría usar dispositivos económicos y poco protegidos para ejecutar su código y continuar propagándose. No le haría falta un centro de datos; solo necesitaría una red de dispositivos conectados a internet y relativamente poco protegidos. articles.title: Cyberattaque « opportuniste » contre les supermarchés français : des chercheurs évoquent « une réalité largement sous-estimée »
articles.summary:
Des équipements industriels connectés, comme des frigos, peuvent être pris pour cible « avec une facilité déconcertante ». Synacktiv, une entreprise française spécialisée dans la cybersécurité offensive, réagit aux cyberattaques qui ont déréglé les frigos de centaines de supermarchés. Pour Synacktiv, la vague de cyberattaques met en lumière « une réalité largement sous-estimée ».
Des failles connues dans les systèmes de Danfoss
Dans une réaction adressée à 01net, l’entreprise assure que ses chercheurs « connaissent particulièrement bien ces systèmes ». Par le passé, les chercheurs de Synacktiv ont déjà identifié plusieurs vulnérabilités dans des équipements signés Danfoss, le fabricant danois au cœur de la cyberattaque contre les supermarchés. L’entreprise originaire du Danemark a en effet conçu les systèmes de régulation frigorifique qui ont été piratés dans la nuit du 11 au 12 octobre 2026, et qui ont été déréglés à distance par des cybercriminels.
Parmi les vulnérabilités épinglées par Synacktiv, on trouve une faille permettant de contourner l’authentification. Autrement dit, des pirates pouvaient se connecter à des systèmes sans avoir besoin du moindre identifiant. L’alerte est loin d’être récente. Trois ans avant la cyberattaque, Synacktiv a déjà découvert des vulnérabilités sur d’anciens systèmes de régulation Danfoss, les SM800 et SC255/SC355. « Le problème est loin d’être théorique », insiste Synacktiv.

articles.title: Hypersonic Technologies is turning methane into hydrogen and carbon black
articles.summary:
Hypersonic Technologies is turning methane into hydrogen and carbon black
Chennai-based deeptech startup Hypersonic Technologies is betting on two revenue streams to help industrial customers offset production costs while reducing emissions.
Hydrogen is expected to play a larger role in helping industries cut emissions, but conventional production methods can leave a significant carbon footprint. Chennai-based Hypersonic Technologies is working on an alternative that produces hydrogen alongside carbon black, a commercially useful material used in tyres, rubber and pigments.
Founded in 2023 by Jayaraman Kandasamy and Jayakumar Venkatesan, the climate-tech startup uses staged-plasma pyrolysis to convert methane and biomethane into hydrogen and solid carbon. By producing two materials through one process, it aims to help industrial customers offset production costs while reducing emissions.
Kandasamy has more than a decade of experience in Europe, where he worked on plasma technology for aerospace propulsion and explored converting biomass into fuel and hydrogen-rich gases. After returning to India, he founded Hypersonic Technologies to apply this experience to industrial decarbonisation.

articles.title: Under the hood, off the hot path: how D1 scales to millions of databases
articles.summary:
Under the hood, off the hot path: How D1 scales to millions of databases
Traditional database architecture assumes you have one or two big database clusters per application, usually accompanied by a connection pooling solution. AI-assisted development and vibe coding platforms turn this model inside out and are driving applications toward many small databases: one per user, application, preview environment, or tenant.
That model fits D1 particularly well. D1 is Cloudflare's managed, serverless database based on SQLite. It allows you to create millions of databases and only pay for what you use.
The question becomes: how do you scale the control plane for millions of databases without making every query slower by sending it through centralized bottlenecks?
We made a lot of architectural changes to scale out D1 to support platforms with millions of created databases, hundreds of thousands of which are active at any point.
This post is a behind-the-scenes deep dive into how the D1 control plane works. Many of the architectural patterns we will describe can be used by anyone building on top of Cloudflare’s Developer Platform. The post also gives a glimpse into how we build our own control planes.
Growth in numbers
There was already a steady growth in D1 usage when we started planning these changes, but we knew we would need to support a much bigger scale once large platforms started building with D1.

articles.title: WhatsApp va enfin vous laisser programmer vos messages
articles.summary:
La fonctionnalité semble anodine et pourtant il aura fallu attendre des années avant de la voir implémentée. Pour certains testeurs utilisant la version bêta de WhatsApp sur Android, il est enfin possible de planifier l'envoi d'un message. Les textes, les liens, les photos ou les vidéos partiront à l'heure choisie, même si le téléphone est hors ligne.
Pouvoir planifier un message, c'est quand même bien pratique, notamment pour gérer les fuseaux horaires ou écrire en dehors des heures de bureau. Si une telle option est disponible depuis longtemps pour les emails, sur les messageries mobiles, cela reste anecdotique. Les utilisateurs réclament cette option depuis longtemps. Telegram la propose déjà, et WhatsApp vient de l'intégrer à sa bêta Android 2.26.40.7.
Entre 10 minutes et deux semaines, vous choisissez l'heure d'envoi
Pour planifier un envoi, il suffit de rédiger son message, puis d'appuyer longuement sur le bouton d'envoi, comme sur Telegram. Une fenêtre apparaît en bas de l'écran pour choisir la date et l'heure. Le message part ensuite tout seul à l'horaire prévu, même si l'application est fermée ou si le téléphone est hors ligne. L'envoi doit être programmé 10 minutes à l'avance au minimum, ce qui laisse le temps de se corriger. Le maximum est de deux semaines. Cela permet par exemple de prévoir un message dans la journée ou de souhaiter un anniversaire en avance.

articles.title: Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock
SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 is now available on Amazon Bedrock, which offers a choice of foundation models (FMs) from multiple providers. According to SpaceXAI, Grok 4.7 is trained to work longer on more difficult tasks and knows when to check its own work. That matters most for agents, which carry a task through many steps and must verify what they find along the way.
An agent that works this way has to do more than look things up. It has to form a candidate answer, check it against what it has learned, and refine it until it fits. Grok 4.7 exposes a reasoning effort setting that controls how much deliberation happens before each response, and for agent workloads a practical question is which level to run.
In this post, we build a tool-calling agent on Grok 4.7 and evaluate it on three tasks that require search rather than lookup. The tasks are diagnosing a two-service outage from its alerts, scheduling maintenance under interacting constraints, and choosing an optimal set of migrations under a budget. Each task has exactly one correct answer, verified by brute force. We ran all three at every reasoning effort level, six times each, for 72 agent runs.

GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
GitHub’s context-aware secret classifier improves detection quality, raises weighted acceptance by 11.5%, and reduces median scan execution time by 86%.

Secret scanning works best when developers are confident in the findings. Catch too little, and real credentials can remain in a repository. Alert too often, and developers may spend time investigating strings that aren’t secrets.
Generic secrets make that balance especially difficult. The same string could be a real credential or a documentation placeholder, so detecting it requires understanding the surrounding code and text.
To address this challenge, we trained a secret classifier specifically for GitHub’s product needs: distinguishing real credentials from lookalikes while meeting the speed and efficiency requirements of scanning at scale.
In our companion post, Secret protection must scale with software, we explained why secret protection must keep pace with AI-accelerated development. articles.title: Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio join 400 scientists calling for international AI regulator | BetaKit
articles.summary:
More than 400 members of the scientific community are pushing for an international AI regulator to curb cybersecurity incidents.
The news: The open letter, released on Tuesday, calls for the creation of an international body to standardize AI containment practices and record and track containment failures. The letter recommends that every security incident involving containment failure be reported to the body and eventually made public, arguing that such transparency is required for learning and accountability.
The open letter counted signatories from all over the world, including nearly 70 Canadians, such as Nobel Prize winner Geoffrey Hinton and Turing Award winner Yoshua Bengio. Both AI pioneers have signed many previous open letters warning about AI’s potentially devastating effects.
From the source: “As scientists, we thought that the current situation with AI models breaking containment during testing was a concern,” University of Toronto professor and signatory David Lie told BetaKit over the phone. “We drafted this letter after talking with people across both the AI and security communities in hopes it would improve the situation.”
The context: The new open letter’s recommendations follow an OpenAI model escaping its test environment and breaching the systems of Hugging Face and other platforms this past summer. That incident was just the first in a growing number of similar disclosures.

articles.title: The Xteink X4 Pro is a great, tiny e-reader, and it’s cheaper than ever
articles.summary:

El ataque alcanzó al menos 300 establecimientos de Intermarché y Netto, más de 100 de Coopérative U y varios de E.Leclerc; Carrefour ha comunicado 80 supermercados afectados.
No sabemos quién lo hizo ni si hubo IA implicada. Pero lo importante de este caso no depende de eso. Porque es un ejemplo de manual de lo que ya permite la IA.
Por qué es importante. Cuando hablamos de los riesgos de la IA pensamos en cosas de película de ciencia-ficción. Pero el problema real, el que ya podemos ver este año, se parece más a este caso: algo medio aburrido, físico y barato de hacer, pero con consecuencias destructivas.
El contexto. El fallo no es nuevo. Danfoss, el fabricante de los controladores, ha reconocido que algunos de los controladores afectados ya no reciben actualizaciones, y que ya hubo ataques parecidos en supermercados de Rusia e Israel en 2022.
La diferencia con aquellos ataques es la escala. Antes eran casos sueltos, pero ahora hablamos de más de 500 tiendas en una noche.
Entre líneas. Estos aparatos llevan años “protegidos” porque atacarlos daba mucha pereza: había que encontrarlos uno a uno, entender un software extraño y adaptar el ataque a cada versión. Ese trabajo tedioso, casi disuasorio, es justo lo que la IA abarata.

The SAP Python SDK is the official programmatic toolkit for developing AI agents and Python applications on the company's SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) services.
Tracked as CVE-2026-89111, the maximum-severity vulnerability patched this month can be exploited by remote attackers without privileges to steal credentials.
Customers who can't immediately deploy the October 2026 SAP patches can temporarily mitigate the issue by using an allowlist to validate tenant_subdomain values.
"The SAP Cloud SDK for Python contains an OAuth2 SSRF vulnerability affecting multi-tenant BTP applications. An attacker who controls the tenant_subdomain parameter can redirect OAuth2 token requests to an attacker-controlled server, causing client credentials to be exfiltrated," according to a Tuesday advisory.
"Consumer applications can mitigate the vulnerability by validating tenant_subdomain against a known allowlist of registered tenant subdomains before passing it to any SDK call."
Today, SAP also addressed CVE-2026-89110, a critical broken access control vulnerability in the SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer that could let remote attackers with limited privileges fully compromise vulnerable systems.

articles.title: Enterprise IT infrastructure isn’t built for AI inference
articles.summary:
Enterprise IT infrastructure isn’t built for AI inference
AI inference requires fundamentally new, distributed enterprise infrastructure
As global AI investment continues to climb — it surpassed $300 billion in 2025, according to IDC — enterprise IT remains primarily focused on supporting the development of training models, with architecture such as large GPU clusters and high-density compute taking center stage.
But now AI inference is becoming the dominant workload, and the architecture that supports models in production, at scale, and to real users and systems has quickly become the future of AI.
The demand for AI inference is there — according to Deloitte, inference already accounts for roughly two-thirds of compute, while McKinsey projects that it will represent between 30% and 40% of total data center demand by 2030 — however, the dedicated infrastructure is not.
CEO of Megaport.
Inference is more than a scaled-down training environment
What training and inference require from an IT point of view are very nearly polar opposites. Enterprises have facilitated AI training via data centers with massive, centralized data GPU clusters for extreme power density and specialized, high-speed interconnects meant to maximize communication within a single room.

articles.title: Europe’s Advanced Packaging Gap: Fraunhofer, Swissbit Target the Missing Middle - EE Times
articles.summary:
Europe has no shortage of semiconductor research. The harder problem often begins after the prototype works.
A company may need an advanced packaging process for a specialized product, but only at volumes of tens, hundreds, or thousands of units. That can be too much for a research organization to support indefinitely and far too little to interest a conventional high-volume outsourced semiconductor assembly and test provider.
Rolf Aschenbrenner, deputy director of the Fraunhofer Institute for Reliability and Microintegration (IZM), sees that gap regularly. “Companies come to us because their volume is too low to get access to advanced packaging,” he told EE Times. “We can help with prototypes, and in some cases we can also do small-volume manufacturing.”
That doesn’t mean Fraunhofer wants to become an outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider. Its role, according to Aschenbrenner, is to adapt packaging processes to customer requirements, demonstrate their viability, and ultimately hand them off to industry. “The goal is that we also transfer our processes,” he said.
The problem is what happens when no industrial manufacturer is ready to take them.
Too small for the OSATs
Aschenbrenner cited fan-out wafer-level packaging as an example. A company developing RF products might require only around 100 wafers per year. For a large packaging provider, that volume barely registers.

articles.title: Microrganismo com genoma minúsculo desafia definição do que é estar vivo
articles.summary:
Um microrganismo com um dos menores genomas já identificados pela ciência está levando pesquisadores a questionar os limites do que caracteriza a vida. Batizado de Sukunaarchaeum mirabile, ele possui apenas 238 mil pares de bases de DNA e apresenta uma estrutura genética tão reduzida que pode depender de outro organismo para sobreviver.
A descoberta aconteceu por acaso, durante uma pesquisa com o plâncton unicelular Citharistes regius, coletado em águas superficiais do mar na costa de Shimoda, no Japão. Os cientistas investigavam o material genético de cianobactérias que vivem em associação com esse plâncton quando encontraram uma pequena sequência circular de DNA que chamou a atenção da equipe.
O estudo foi publicado na revista científica Current Biology e reúne pesquisadores das áreas de biologia e ciência da computação.
Organismo tem menos DNA do que alguns vírus
- O Sukunaarchaeum mirabile pertence ao domínio Archaea, formado por organismos unicelulares que, assim como as bactérias, não possuem o DNA protegido por um núcleo envolvido por membrana. Apesar dessas semelhanças, as arqueias têm uma história evolutiva própria e características distintas das bactérias;
- O tamanho do genoma recém-identificado é particularmente impressionante. Existem vírus com genomas maiores do que o do microrganismo, alguns com 730 mil pares de bases e outros com até 2,5 milhões;
- A comparação chama a atenção porque os vírus não são considerados seres vivos por muitas definições convencionais…

Sana, which Workday bought for $1.1 billion last year, is available now, and admins can roll it out to their users without making it the default.
Picking components instead of writing them

Workday gave Jev every atomic component in its design system and hard-coded none of the selection logic, Hellermark said, though the team also had to get data preloading right. In the demo, the paycheck card appeared before he finished typing, for example.

articles.title: AI Turns Familiar Cyberattacks Into a Race Against Time
articles.summary:
In the AI era, phishing remains the top attack vector in both use (17% of breaches) and breach costs (averaging at $5.29 per breach) according to the IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026. AI creates more personalized content for phishing with higher success rates. At the same time, AI can identify vulnerabilities, use the phished entry point and elevate privileges for lateral movement at greater speed.
None of this is new – cyberattacks haven’t changed with AI. “It just allows attackers to do the same familiar things much faster and at greater scale than ever before. The pressure comes from minimizing the time for defenders to respond,” says Steve Wallin, director of core integration and R&D labs leader at IBM UK.
For now, AI-generated attacks are still in the minority – little more than 20% of all attacks. But the writing (written by AI) is on the wall, and it is incumbent on enterprises to improve their security defenses now before the tsunami arrives in full.
SecurityWeek talked to Wallin on how enterprises should respond to this growing AI threat. Again, it is nothing new – it must just be done better.
It starts with a basic maxim that is as old as the ancient Delphic Oracle: ‘know thyself’. “Organizations must understand their existing security posture. The key to defending against this increasing volume of attacks and decreasing time to respond is again nothing new. It means focusing on proactive rather than reactive defense. It is security by design from the ground up…

The exec talked about Pascal's quote of how there is a God-shaped vacuum, or hole, in the heart of every person, and how many AI workers in Silicon Valley had filled that hole with the machine god that is AI (or AGI, as he calls it).
As an example of this unwavering faith in their Warhammer 40,000-like machine god, Sankar claims that many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI.

articles.title: The MFA Gaps Attackers are Still Exploiting
articles.summary:
On August 4, 2026, an Akira ransomware affiliate began spraying passwords against a SonicWall SSL VPN. Around seven minutes later, one attempt succeeded. The credentials were valid, and the VPN account had no multi-factor authentication (MFA) protecting it. Roughly two hours later, the attacker used RDP to access the domain controller and began enumerating Active Directory.
The ransomware deployment ultimately failed, but by then the attacker had already stolen credentials and file-share data.
It highlights an issue that is still common in 2026, where an organization might require MFA for Microsoft 365 and other SaaS applications while leaving certain access paths protected only by passwords. It’s this gap that attackers are regularly exploiting.
Stolen Credentials Remain a Valuable Tool for Attackers
Once an attacker has a valid account, they can begin interacting with the environment through the same authentication mechanisms used by legitimate employees and administrators. AI is adding another dimension to this problem by helping attackers operate at greater speed and scale.
The underlying identity tactics are largely unchanged: attackers still compromise identities, reuse credentials, escalate privileges and misuse legitimate access. The threat is that AI makes familiar techniques cheaper and easier to run at scale.

articles.title: This Chennai startup is building a device to help doctors choose the right antibiotic sooner
articles.summary:
This Chennai startup is building a device to help doctors choose the right antibiotic sooner
Attox Research Laboratories is developing a testing device that shows which antibiotic will work on a patient's infection, and at what dose.
When a patient arrives with a bacterial infection, doctors may have to choose an antibiotic before laboratory tests confirm which one will work. A sensitivity test checks which antibiotic can kill the bacteria in a patient’s sample, but standard testing takes 24 to 48 hours. The first prescription, including the dose, therefore often relies on an assumption.
That has consequences beyond the first few days of treatment. Antibiotics taken when they are not needed, or in excess, contribute to antimicrobial resistance, making the drugs less effective against bacteria.
Chennai-based Attox Research Laboratories is developing a device to shorten that wait. Its flagship product, the Bactolizer, is designed to identify the effective antibiotic and the correct dose from a list of 15 antibiotics in about 30 minutes to two hours.
Attox was founded in 2023 by Clement, Suganth and Senthil. Clement holds an MBA and has more than 18 years of experience in startup building and organisational management. Suganth holds a Bachelor of Pharmacy degree and was an undergraduate researcher under Senthil, who has a PhD in analytical chemistry and more than 20 years of experience in teaching and research.
"We ideally want the first antibiotic to be the right antibiotic," C…

articles.title: The era of passwords is coming to an end

The era of passwords is coming to an end
Passkeys are quickly replacing passwords
Discussions about passkeys replacing passwords as the go-to sign-in method have rapidly accelerated. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) has acted as the catalyst for this transition, describing the shift as "overhauling decades of security practice". Finally, the industry has reached a collective point of recognition: traditional, static passwords are a weak defense against modern, automated threats.
Alex Laurie is GTM CTO at Ping Identity.
AI has turned cybercrime into a highly efficient, industrial-scale enterprise. With researchers uncovering agentic ransomware attacks, we are fast approaching a reality that outpaces traditional human-centric defenses. Cybercriminals routinely deploy industrial-scale AI tooling to orchestrate and deploy vast credential-stuffing attacks and hyper-realistic phishing campaigns at machine speed and scale.
For organizations, the adoption of passkeys and other passwordless verification methods is dependent on the maturity of existing identity and access management (IAM) systems. Of the businesses with less mature, or no IAM strategy in place, only 30% are embracing password alternatives. Without passwordless systems, threat actors will continue to undermine digital trust.

He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around $15,000) for the workspace data in Google, Notion, Figma, and Slack. “At least all that stuff we were doing for two and a half years is worth something to someone somewhere,” he says.
The sale was brokered by a company called SimpleClosure, part of a new growth sector in tech: businesses catering to dying startups. Estimates from Carta and AngelList show shutdowns rising between 26% and 56% annually in recent years, and an end-of-life ecosystem—including coaches, “death doulas,” and firms that help handle the legal, tax, and operational headaches of going belly-up—has emerged. articles.title: Docker Hub flaw let attackers impersonate users, tamper with images
articles.summary:
Docker has disclosed a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-105445) in Docker Hub that let attackers access another user’s container repositories using a personal access token (PAT).
Docker Hub is an online registry for storing, sharing, and downloading container images - templates that package everything needed for an application to run in an isolated environment.
In Docker Hub, a PAT serves as a secret used to authenticate tools and workflows. It allows you to pull, push, or delete container images.
According to a security bulletin from the Docker team, an attacker could create an account and PAT, then convert the account into an organization and name a target user as its owner.
The CVE-2026-105445 flaw stems from Docker Hub reassigning a personal access token (PAT) to a designated organization owner without changing its secret or obtaining the target's consent. This allowed the attacker to use the token to authenticate as the target.
Depending on the token’s scope and the target’s permissions, attackers could pull, push, or delete images in the target’s repositories and accessible organizations.
“Within the scope of the token, a re-assigned PAT acted as the target user at the registry level, meaning an attacker could potentially pull, push, and/or delete images in the target’s repositories and in organizations where the target had access,” Docker explained.

Les annonceurs surenchérissent alors en une fraction de seconde pour afficher leur publicité. Xandr y participait côté offre comme côté achat. articles.title: Un robot camina sin batería gracias a un truco: usar el suelo como energía
articles.summary:
Un pequeño robot caminante logró moverse durante 150 días sin depender de ninguna batería convencional. La clave está en una membrana instalada en sus patas, capaz de generar electricidad cada vez que toca una superficie metálica. El desarrollo, liderado por Yue Gao, del Departamento de Ciencia Macromolecular de la Universidad Fudan, se publicó en la revista National Science Review.
El problema de fondo es conocido en la robótica miniaturizada: cuanto más chico es un robot, menos espacio queda disponible para una batería, y las que logran entrar ofrecen muy poca autonomía.
Un robot de menos de dos gramos con una batería comercial apenas se sostiene en movimiento un par de minutos. Frente a esa limitación, el equipo de Fudan decidió invertir la lógica y convertir el propio terreno en fuente de energía.
Cómo funciona la membrana que convierte el suelo en energía
El mecanismo se apoya en una membrana de gel de poliacrilato de potasio, un polímero que retiene agua y que mide apenas 135 micrómetros de espesor, un grosor comparable al de una hoja de papel. Ese material se coloca en las patas del robot y entra en acción cada vez que hay contacto con el suelo.
Cuando la pata pisa una superficie de aluminio, zinc o silicio, se desencadena una reacción electroquímica. El metal del piso cede electrones, mientras que el oxígeno y la humedad del aire los reciben del otro lado de la membrana. El suelo pasa a funcionar como uno de los componentes de una pila, de manera similar a las batería…

More than 20 percent of the MCP-related access policies that Shawn Petty’s team reviewed across customer and prospect environments were broken or missing, according to a recent account published in The New Stack. In most cases, the MCP server ran on someone’s personal token rather than a service account.
At 12 p.m. Eastern/9 a.m. Pacific on Tuesday, October 27, Petty, Chief Customer Officer at CloudBolt, and Mike Bombard, Director of Global Pre-Sales Engineering at CloudBolt, will join The New Stack host Viktor Farcic for a live demo of how to trace an agent’s actions back to the person responsible for them.
You have successfully registered for the webinar.
The problem, though, usually shows up after an incident: That personal token puts an engineer’s name into the audit trail for everything the agent did. Meanwhile, a shared service account puts the account’s name there instead. In both cases, the audit trail isn’t able to identify who precisely asked the agent to do the work or who approved the access it used.
Access that goes through a request, approval, and grant in the identity provider is provisioned, and the identity provider records it. The malware’s developers have been constantly updating its codebase and adding new functionality, and the threat has remained highly active, with Netskope observing over 1,200 incidents across 100 organizations during the third quarter of the year.

L’iPhone Duo, premier pliant d’Apple, doit gérer la chaleur d’une puce gravée en 2 nm dans un châssis en deux parties. Selon un entretien accordé par Apple à PCMag, la charnière joue ici un rôle thermique inattendu : elle sert de pont pour répartir la chaleur sur une plus grande surface.
Un conduit de graphite flexible traverse la charnière
Banafsheh Barabadi, responsable senior de la conception thermique chez Apple, qualifie ce point de « l’un des aspects techniquement les plus difficiles » du design. Le conduit transfère la chaleur d’une moitié de l’appareil à l’autre, ce qui augmente la surface disponible pour la dissiper. Sur un pliant, l’épaisseur double une fois l'appareil refermé, d’où l’intérêt de mettre les deux moitiés à contribution.
La pièce a dû être conçue conjointement par les équipes thermique et mécanique. Il s’agit d’un matériau flexible qui doit encaisser de très nombreux cycles d’ouverture tout en conservant sa conductivité thermique et son intégrité structurelle sur toute la vie du produit. Autrement dit, la même pièce doit être un bon conducteur et un bon ressort, deux qualités qui s’accordent rarement.

articles.title: Ivanti warns of Connect Secure zero-day exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
Ivanti urged customers on Tuesday to immediately patch an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability in the Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway.
Formerly known as Pulse Connect Secure and originally Juniper Pulse, the enterprise-grade ICS SSL VPN provides remote employees, contractors, and hybrid workforces with secure access to corporate and cloud resources.
Tracked as CVE-2026-104935, this high-severity authentication bypass zero-day affects ICS versions 22.8R2.4 and earlier, 25.1.2.2 and earlier, and 25.1.1.1 and earlier.
Remote threat actors without privileges can exploit CVE-2026-104935 in low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction to execute arbitrary commands on targeted ICS appliances.
"At the time of disclosure, Ivanti is aware of limited exploitation in the wild. We are working directly with those organizations while making information, updates and remediation available to the broader customer community. If you are running one of the impacted versions, Ivanti recommends you act immediately," Ivanti said.
"Customers should review the security advisory, upgrade to the fixed version as soon as possible, and run the Integrity Checker Tool regularly."
Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver now tracks over 5,500 ICS instances exposed online, but there is no information on how many are honeypots or have already been secured against ongoing attacks.
Exploited since at least October 3

Digitaler Ausweis auf dem Smartphone: Was Banken an der d-you-Wallet kritisieren
Die staatliche Wallet „d-you“ soll im Januar 2027 starten. Nutzer können sich damit per Smartphone ausweisen, amtliche Dokumente speichern und elektronisch unterschreiben.
Grundlage dafür ist die EU-Verordnung eIDAS 2.0, die jeden Mitgliedstaat verpflichtet, seinen Bürgern eine solche Wallet anzubieten. Die Bundesregierung plant dazu entsprechende Regeln im Digitale Identitätengesetz (DIdG), über den Gesetzentwurf stimmt der Bundestag voraussichtlich am Donnerstag ab.
Die Deutsche Kreditwirtschaft (DK), als Interessenvertretung der Banken und Sparkassen, fordert nun Nachschärfungen im Gesetz. Zwar begrüßen die Banken, dass Kunden sich künftig per Wallet geldwäscherechtlich identifizieren können, wenn sie ein Konto eröffnen. Die Institute fordern jedoch, klar festzulegen, dass es ausreicht, die vom Wallet–Verfahren bereitgestellten Daten zu speichern, also dass eine Ausweiskopie weder erforderlich noch technisch umsetzbar ist. Ohne diese Präzisierung könnten Banken sonst vorsichtshalber zusätzliche Nachweise verlangen, wodurch der Vorteil einer schnellen, papierlosen Kontoeröffnung verloren gehen könnte.
Außerdem müsse das Gesetz klarer regeln, wann Banken eine fremde Wallet akzeptieren müssen, wer bei technischen Fehlern haftet und welche Daten ihnen zur Betrugsabwehr zur Verfügung stehen.

Endeavor Catalyst, the venture capital arm of global entrepreneur network Endeavor, has closed its oversubscribed Fund V at US$320 million, taking its total assets under management past US$850 million.
Endeavor Catalyst invests exclusively in companies led by Endeavor Entrepreneurs, co-investing alongside leading venture capital and growth equity firms. Across its five funds, it has already backed 437 companies in 44 markets, deploying more than US$500 million across 469 investments.
Africa makes up seven per cent of both the portfolio and Catalyst capital, with 29 companies backed across five African markets, including the likes of Flutterwave, Moniepoint, MAX and Moove. Six of these are valued at US$1 billion or more. A decade ago, the fund had made no African investments.

CXMT expects to sell a memory cell that Samsung and SK hynix have only shown in research papers so far.
CXMT expects to launch its first 4F² product, a server DDR5 RDIMM, by the end of the year, company president Cao Kanyu said in remarks reported by Yicai. The memory will be built on a denser cell layout, not yet commercialized, using vertical transistors to reduce the cell’s footprint by about one-third on paper. No speeds or capacities have been announced yet for the new product.
Cao spoke about the new RDIMM at the Integrated Chips and Chiplets Conference on Saturday. A 4F² cell is 2F by 2F at about two-thirds the area of current 6F² cells at the same feature size, and designs so far all stand the transistor up. The company has produced research and patent filings on the technology with papers in 2021, 2023, and 2025, and an 8Gb full-array research example was demonstrated at IEDM 2023.
Cao said CXMT’s version, the Vertical Surrounded Gate (VSG) transistor, has a channel that stands vertically with the gate wrapped around it, allowing stronger gate control with less leakage. Most importantly, standing the transistor up shrinks the cell. CXMT now has more than 300 published patent families tied to 4F², he added. Watching the Bitcoin price gives founders a sense of what is happening in the market, but it does not tell them whether crypto belongs in their own business.
Bitcoin crossed €74,222 ($85,000) on September 22 after ETF inflows hit €539.9 million ($617.6 million) in the previous session, according to Reuters reporting published by The Economic Times. That kind of movement is hard to ignore. It is also not necessarily the information a founder needs when deciding whether to adopt digital assets.
The better question is much more practical: where, if anywhere, could crypto make running a startup easier?
Why are startups exploring crypto?
Part of the interest comes down to how blockchain networks operate. They can run continuously, and digital assets can move between countries without following exactly the same route as a conventional bank payment.
For a young company working internationally, that can be interesting. A customer could be based in one country, contractors in another and suppliers somewhere else. Add different currencies and banking systems to the mix, and moving money can become even more complex.

articles.title: The traditional PC layout might not be the best: unusual GPU placement cuts temperatures by 17°C

In a nutshell: PC builders have long tried to find the most optimal cooling setups for their components, moving around fans, cables, etc. to find the best configurations. A YouTube channel decided to try something a little different: moving the components themselves. This included shifting the GPU next to a case's side-intake, which resulted in a 17-degree drop in temperatures.
The experiment was carried out by TrashBench, which used an Asus ROG Strix RTX 3080 inside a dual-chamber case. The cooling came from three side-intake fans, a rear exhaust, and a top-mounted 360mm CPU AIO.
The idea was to change component placement without moving the case fans. PCIe riser cables were used so the graphics card could be moved away from its usual slot on the motherboard.
Testing involved looping 3DMark Time Spy alongside 7-Zip running on 12 CPU threads. All fans stayed at fixed RPMs, with each configuration tested for ten minutes and temperatures averaged over the final five.
The GPU's first position was on the case floor, which required the removal of the bottom mesh because it touched the card's fans. GPU temperatures barely changed, but the CPU and motherboard VRM dropped around 4°C and 7°C, respectively. Conventional vertical mounting slightly worsened GPU temperatures while modestly improving everything else.
However, placing the card directly against the side intake made all the difference. GPU core temperatures fell 16.7°C, the hotspot dropped 19.3°C, and VRAM cooled by 14°C. Moth…

The dispute centres on two shareholder demands. Investors holding approximately 76% of ABC’s shares called for the appointment of two new non-executive directors, a move the board opposed on governance grounds. articles.title: Cloudflare’s OHTTP Gateway Refuses to Decrypt Requests That Arrive Through Cloudflare
articles.summary:
Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of the Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway, a managed endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP requests on an origin’s behalf. The design decision that drew most of the attention is a refusal rather than a feature: the Gateway will not decrypt requests that reach it from Cloudflare Workers or from hosts proxied through Cloudflare.
Oblivious HTTP, standardized as RFC 9458, splits a request across two parties. The client encrypts the inner HTTP request to the gateway’s public key using HPKE and sends the sealed payload to a relay. The relay sees the client’s IP address but cannot read the request. The gateway decrypts it and forwards plain HTTP to the application, so it sees the contents but only ever sees the relay’s address.
That only works if different operators run the two hops. Putting a Worker in front of the Gateway, or proxying the relay through Cloudflare, would route the client-identifying hop and the decryption hop through the same company, so Cloudflare built a product that declines to run in that configuration. Authors Lara Schull and Akshat Mahajan write that the model "requires that the relay and app server be operated by separate, non-colluding parties."
For a team evaluating this, the practical cost is the relay. Cloudflare does not supply one for the Gateway, and says the component is not the hard part, since relays "can run on any infrastructure provider, and they’re simple." The hard part is being in a position to "verifiably promise to…

articles.title: Small AI Models Could Soon Self-Replicate on IoT Devices, Anthropic Warns
articles.summary:
Small AI models may be only months away from being able to self-replicate across commercial IoT devices, without needing a data center, according to research from Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team.
The study looks at AI worms that run their own model directly on the devices they compromise. Such malware would be hard to shut down because it has no central point to switch off, though it would likely spread slowly.
The researchers bought 15 off-brand Android-based TV boxes for about $55 each. A 26-billion-parameter open-weight model split across them ran at 0.39 tokens per second.
Rather than exploitation, which prior studies have already examined, the team focused on whether models could get AI inference running on unfamiliar hardware. A 9-billion-parameter model did so on eight of the nine hardware types tested.
The researchers then tested the full replication cycle on a closed network of eight emulated Android devices, with the hacking step deliberately kept trivial. Of the open-weight models tested, only GLM-5.2 completed it, reaching all eight devices in four of five runs.
Anthropic considers the results an upper bound for real-world success, but notes that past IoT botnets such as Mirai spread simply by trying default manufacturer credentials.
Models with 30 billion parameters or fewer can already complete many of the individual steps but make mistakes when chaining them together. If they keep improving at their historical rate, Anthropic expects them to reach GLM-5.2’s level…

articles.title: High-speed video reveals how honey bee stingers pump venom
articles.summary:
Honey bees are known to leave their stingers embedded in tender flesh once they sting you and fly away. Scientists have now determined that the stinger is able to continue pumping venom into its unfortunate victim even after the bee flies away, thanks to a unique double-piston pump-like mechanism, according to a new paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
Different species have evolved different mechanisms for delivering venom, which involves piercing the skin and then pumping venom from a gland or reservoir. Spiders, for instance, have muscles surrounding their venom glands, which contract and eject venom through hollow fangs. Bees, wasps, and ants deliver venom via their stingers, either by contracting muscles around the venom reservoir or through stiff elements called lancets working together to pump venom.
Honey bees (Apis mellifera) add a unique feature: Worker bees fly away after inserting their stingers in the target, leaving the stinger behind. The stinger continues to penetrate the tissue and pump venom on its own, a rare phenomenon known as autotomy. A honey bee’s stinger has three main interlocking elements that form the venom canal: a stylet that widens to form the main pumping chamber and two sharp-tipped lancets that slide back and forth, piercing the tissue and pumping venom into the target. But the precise mechanism by which the pumping action is achieved has never been directly observed.

articles.title: Anthropic’s red team ran AI on 15 cheap TV boxes. Then the math got unsettling.
articles.summary:
Anthropic’s red team ran AI on 15 cheap TV boxes. Then the math got unsettling.
For roughly $825, Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team built a cluster of 15 off-brand Android TV boxes that runs an AI model at 0.39 tokens per second, painfully slow for a chatbot but fine for software with nowhere to be and nobody waiting on it.
That experiment anchors new research from Anthropic researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman, published Monday, suggesting small open-weight models may be only months away from copying themselves across cheap, internet-connected hardware without relying on a datacenter.
The researchers haven’t built an AI worm that can spread across the public internet on its own, and their experiments took place inside controlled environments with shortcuts that made replication easier. But the results suggest several of the remaining technical barriers may be temporary.
The researchers haven’t built an AI worm that can spread across the public internet on its own, and their experiments took place inside controlled environments with shortcuts that made replication easier.

Selon le cabinet d’étude, la demande reste soutenue sur le haut de gamme, mais le milieu et l’entrée de gamme ont plus de mal. Deux gammes de prix qui demandent un rapport qualité-prix que ne peuvent plus offrir les marques, ou du moins pas au niveau d’avant la crise de la RAM.

AI has been changing the pace and profile of vulnerability discovery, and the tech giant has been adjusting its bug bounty programs in recent months.
Google significantly lowered standard payout amounts for some Chrome vulnerabilities in April to shift focus to actionable reports, with researchers noting that some rewards became 10 times smaller. At the time it announced a base reward of $500 for memory safety issues, with multipliers for reachability and the level of exploitability.
The company is now quadrupling base rates for memory safety flaws, to $2,000. Despite the increase, the new rates remain well below those offered before the April overhaul.
Vulnerabilities in Chrome’s browser, GPU and network processes can now earn researchers up to $20,000. In the case of the renderer process, bug bounty hunters can receive up to $8,000 for use-after-free and memory write bugs.
V8 sandbox vulnerabilities are moving to a flat rate of $5,000, while V8 logic bugs will be rewarded with $4,000.
As for issues not related to memory safety, medium-severity flaws will be rewarded with $2,000 if the vulnerability report includes or directly leads to an identified fix. Sandbox escapes not involving memory safety bugs can get bug bounties of up to $20,000.
Google is also reintroducing a $2,000 fuzzer bonus for developing novel fuzzers.

Ese es el punto de partida de todo el proceso.

El proyecto requiere apenas tres elementos. El primero es el propio control remoto en desuso, que puede ser de cualquier marca o dispositivo, siempre que sus botones y su emisor infrarrojo funcionen con normalidad.

El tercer componente es, naturalmente, la computadora donde se instalará el adaptador, sin importar el sistema operativo que utilice.

articles.title: Rätsel der Monsterwellen gelöst: Wie KI die Gefahr auf See berechenbar macht
articles.summary:
Formel statt Seemannsgarn: KI analysiert die Entstehung von Monsterwellen
Am 17. November 2020 registrierte eine Sensorboje des kanadischen Unternehmens MarineLabs eine Wassersäule, die Ozeanograf:innen weltweit beschäftigte. Das im Pazifik vor der Küste von Ucluelet verankerte Messgerät zeichnete eine Einzelwelle von 17,6 Metern Höhe auf. Das Ereignis sticht deshalb heraus, weil der restliche Seegang zu diesem Zeitpunkt bei lediglich rund sechs Metern lag.
Damit ein solches Ereignis in der Wissenschaft als Monsterwelle (im Fachjargon Rogue Wave genannt) eingestuft wird, ist nicht die absolute Höhe entscheidend, sondern das Verhältnis zur sogenannten signifikanten Wellenhöhe. Dieser Referenzwert beschreibt die Durchschnittshöhe des höchsten Drittels aller Wellen in einem Messzeitraum. Übertrifft eine einzelne Welle diesen Durchschnitt um mehr als das Doppelte gilt sie als Monsterwelle.
Mit dem fast Dreifachen der signifikanten Wellenhöhe ist das Ereignis von Ucluelet proportional die extremste jemals gemessene Welle. Zum Vergleich: Die berühmte Draupner-Welle, die am 1. Januar 1995 an einer norwegischen Ölplattform in der Nordsee den ersten Beweis für die Existenz des Phänomens lieferte, war zwar 25,6 Meter hoch, trat aber in einem schweren Seegang von ohnehin schon zwölf Metern auf.
Warum etablierte Erklärungsmodelle auf dem Ozean versagen

articles.title: AWS Reworks EventBridge Custom Buses for Enterprise-Scale Event-Driven Architectures
articles.summary:
AWS has introduced an enhanced Custom Event Bus for Amazon EventBridge, targeting a problem that often emerges when event-driven architectures move beyond a single team or AWS account: the event infrastructure itself becomes fragmented. The new model allows organisations to create a single event bus shared across multiple AWS accounts, while adding native event ordering, retention and replay, content-based deduplication, simplified subscriptions and a new pricing model.
The change addresses an architectural tension in enterprise AWS environments. Organisations commonly use multiple accounts to provide isolation between teams and applications, but this can lead to EventBridge buses being connected through cross-account rules and forwarding configurations. As the number of consumers grows, the resulting topology becomes harder to govern and understand, while forwarding the same event through multiple buses can introduce additional processing and routing costs. AWS's new model instead positions a central bus as an organisational event backbone, with individual teams managing their own subscriptions.
The enhanced Custom Event Bus can be shared across AWS accounts using AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM). A platform team can therefore establish a central event bus while allowing application teams to publish and subscribe from their own accounts. AWS says the new bus supports up to 10,000 subscribers by default, with the option to request a higher quota.

articles.title: Jonathan es una tortuga, tiene 194 años y acabamos de descubrir por qué su ADN envejece tan lentamente

El secreto de la longevidad extrema siempre ha sido un tema que ha fascinado a la ciencia, pero para saber cómo se puede vivir más de 200 años, a veces no hay que mirar a los humanos, sino a un apacible reptil que lleva caminando por este planeta desde antes que se inventara la bombilla, como es Jonathan. Esta es una tortuga gigante que, a sus 194 años, ostenta el récord de ser el animal terrestre más longevo del mundo.
Su razón. Aguantar durante todos los años hace que la gente busque el porqué. Y aquí la ciencia ha decidido asomarse al interior de sus células gracias a un equipo internacional que ha secuenciado su genoma y su metiloma para entender la razón por la que Jonathan no envejece como el resto de animales.
Un simple frotis. Para entender un poco mejor a Jonathan, no hizo falta someterle a dolorosas pruebas, sino que solo bastó con raspar la mucosa bucal del animal. A partir de esta muestra, un equipo internacional comparó su ADN con el de otras tortugas gigantes de Aldabra mucho más jóvenes.
El resultado. Lo que encontraron en el código genético fue un arsenal biológico muy importante, puesto que se pudieron identificar hasta 287 genes con variantes exclusivas de Jonathan. Pero lo interesante es que muchas de estas variantes están íntimamente ligadas a la supresión de tumores y a la reparación del ADN.

articles.title: Adobe Patches 140 Vulnerabilities Across 10 Products
articles.summary:
Adobe has published 10 new security advisories to inform customers about roughly 140 vulnerabilities found and patched in its products.
Adobe ColdFusion updates address 32 vulnerabilities, including critical bugs that can be exploited for code execution and privilege escalation.
A significant number of flaws have been patched by Adobe in the Content Credentials SDK. The product received fixes for 30 vulnerabilities, many described as high-severity issues that can lead to a security feature bypass. Some security holes can be exploited to cause a DoS condition.
Adobe patched 18 vulnerabilities in Photoshop, nearly all allowing arbitrary code execution.
In Substance 3D Stager, Adobe fixed 16 vulnerabilities, including many high-severity arbitrary code execution flaws.
Eleven vulnerabilities have been resolved in Adobe Commerce, including several critical issues that can be exploited without authentication to execute code or escalate privileges.
Several vulnerabilities that allow arbitrary code execution have been fixed in each of the following products: FrameMaker, Dimension, Substance 3D Sampler, Substance 3D Designer, and Bridge.
Adobe says it’s not aware of any in-the-wild exploitation. Most advisories have a priority rating of 3, which indicates Adobe does not expect to see these vulnerabilities exploited in attacks. Commerce is the only product with a priority rating of 2 (threat actors have historically targeted Commerce).
