articles.title: GTA 6 is reportedly coming to PC in Q1 2027, just months after consoles
articles.summary:
Crystal ball: Rockstar has always made PC players wait for its big releases, sometimes for a year or two. If a new report proves accurate, however, Grand Theft Auto VI could break that pattern. The reason may have less to do with goodwill toward PC gamers and more to do with where GTA's online future is likely to be built.
Rockstar plans to release the PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI as soon as Q1 2027, according to a GamesBeat report citing four industry sources. Rockstar has not responded to requests for comment, and there's no official announcement yet either.
Meanwhile, the long-awaited console version of GTA VI remains on track for November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series. A Q1 2027 PC launch would mean a gap of just a few months.
That would be a sharp break from Rockstar's track record: GTA V launched on consoles in September 2013 and did not reach PC until April 2015, some 19 months later. In the case of Red Dead Redemption 2, the game arrived on consoles in October 2018 and on PC in November 2019.
This new report contradicts the company's public messaging, at least on the surface. In May, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick told Bloomberg that Rockstar "always starts on console" because it needs to serve its core audience first. In the same interview, he acknowledged that PC can account for 45% to 50% of sales on some titles.
Leaked analytics data suggests why Take-Two sees consoles as the core. The data was dumped by ShinyHunters after Rockstar ignored a ransom demand…

articles.title: Production Patterns for Agents, Evals, and LLM Costs: QCon AI New York 2026
articles.summary:
Once AI is in production, code arrives faster than it can be reviewed, token costs rise, evals have to be good enough to act on, and agents need permissions and guardrails. QCon AI New York 2026 has confirmed sessions from senior engineers who have worked through these problems in systems they run. The conference takes place December 15-16 at The Westin Jersey City Newport, about five minutes by PATH train from the World Trade Center. It is for senior engineers and technical leaders making decisions on production AI.
What the sessions offer is hindsight. The senior engineers presenting have already made these decisions and run the results in production. They describe the system and the numbers behind it, letting another team compare an approach against its own constraints before committing.
Identity and authorization for agents in production
The QCon AI opening keynote describes two bad options for giving an agent production access. Teams hand it a long-lived service account and hope, or scope access too narrowly until it cannot finish its task. Nancy Wang, who founded and scaled AWS Data Protection, provides alternative solutions in When Software Becomes a User: Identity and Authorization for Agents in Production.

articles.title: 'I look to China as gurus': Zoho's Sridhar Vembu
articles.summary:
'I look to China as gurus': Zoho's Sridhar Vembu
Speaking at TechSparks 2026, Vembu said India has more to learn from China's technology ecosystem than America's, arguing that technology ownership, rather than engineering talent alone, is essential for lasting economic prosperity.
India should look to China for lessons on building technological capabilities rather than continue relying on a model centred on providing software services to global companies, Zoho Co-founder and Chief Scientist Sridhar Vembu said on Tuesday.
Speaking at YourStory's TechSparks 2026 in Bengaluru, Vembu argued that China had successfully built and retained ownership of critical technologies, allowing it to capture economic value and develop globally competitive businesses. "As much as we think of China as adversaries, I actually look to them as gurus," Vembu said.
"Chinese technology landscape has many more lessons to offer us than America does today," he added.
Vembu said Zoho's own journey had drawn inspiration from East Asian economies, including Japan, Taiwan, South Korea and China, which developed sophisticated technology industries despite constraints involving resources, population density and economic development. He recalled how Chinese engineers visiting Zoho's Chennai operations around 25 years ago were perceived by their Indian counterparts as coming from a poorer country.
"Nobody would say this today," he said, pointing to China's subsequent transformation into a major technology power.…

articles.title: Le créateur de Linux a utilisé Claude Code pour modifier son propre noyau… et c'est une petite révolution
articles.summary:
Linus Torvalds a publié dans son propre dépôt une série de huit patchs pour le noyau Linux, conçue avec Claude Code.
Le créateur de Linux a baptisé sa branche noref-filemap-read-with-llm, et le suffixe dit tout : le code, les programmes de test, la revue des problèmes ouverts et le premier jet de la lettre d'accompagnement viennent de l'assistant d'Anthropic. Les benchmarks, eux, ont tourné sur sa machine. C'est la première fois qu'il crédite un agent pour une série touchant à la gestion mémoire du noyau dans son propre arbre, un cran au-dessus de ses usages précédents, limités au débogage.
Un compteur disputé par tous les cœurs du processeur
Le chantier vise le cache de pages, la zone de mémoire vive où le noyau garde les fichiers récemment lus. Quand plusieurs threads lisent de petits morceaux du même fichier, chaque lecture prend puis relâche une référence sur la page concernée, deux écritures atomiques sur la même ligne de cache. Les cœurs se la disputent.
Les tentatives précédentes copiaient les données dans un tampon sans référence, puis validaient après coup, mais butaient sur des courses que cette validation ne détecte pas, comme une page libérée puis réinsérée au même index. Torvalds supprime plutôt la cause : une page sortie du cache ne retourne à l'allocateur qu'après une période de grâce, ce qui permet à un lecteur de copier directement vers le tampon utilisateur, sans référence ni limite de taille de lecture.

articles.title: Nvidia doubles DLSS 5 performance, reduces 4K VRAM usage by 20% with latest model — October update cuts footprint by 24% to roughly 118 million parameters

Nvidia doubles DLSS 5 performance, reduces 4K VRAM usage by 20% with latest model — October update cuts footprint by 24% to roughly 118 million parameters
A big step.
Nvidia has today announced that its somewhat controversial DLSS 5 technology — AI-powered neural rendering for gaming — is now two times faster than the current model, marking a 10x performance leap since March. The model is also now smaller and uses up to 20% less VRAM.
Nvidia says it has achieved this through a combination of "systematic pipeline optimizations and neural model refinements." As mentioned, the latest performance jump over the current model is a 2x leap, which means that the transformation DLSS applies to games through lighting and beyond will now run at higher frame rates or more intense settings.
Nvidia says the DLSS 5 October update shrinks the overall DLSS 5 model's footprint by nearly a quarter to 118 million parameters, and reduces VRAM usage at 4K by 20%. As such, the company claims that at similar visual fidelity, the GPU overhead versus the September model has been halved. Elsewhere, Nvidia says the change can boost frame rates by up to 1.4x.

articles.title: Gemini 4 Argon begins rolling out in Gemini app and Antigravity, but only if you pay
articles.summary:
Google revealed Gemini 4 Argon a few weeks ago, saying that it needed to move cautiously toward a full release because of the potential for nefarious use. Google seems to have worked all that out pretty quickly, though. Argon is beginning its wide rollout today, but it’s only coming to paying users at this time, and even those on lower-tier plans won’t have full access.
Nothing about Gemini 4 Argon’s capabilities has changed. Google still points to the benchmarks it published late last month as evidence of the model’s advanced reasoning and agentic coding capabilities. The model is supposedly trained to refuse malicious instructions, and an automated misalignment monitor can stop processing if it detects an unintended workflow. Google claims Argon needs that because it’s so capable.
The company has a few new examples of how Argon has helped inside Google, where it has been used by thousands of Googlers. Argon has reportedly been instrumental in making YouTube’s comment system more efficient. Argon identified redundant emoji rendering that, when eliminated, dropped server load by 45 percent. Engineers also turned Gemini 4 loose on the proprietary drone physics simulator used in Project Wing, and the AI found critical bugs that had been in the codebase since 2018. Google also notes that Argon has advanced its robotics program, showing a measurable step increase in embodied reasoning.

articles.title: Ivanti Zero-Day Chain Gave Attackers Root Access to Fully Patched VPN

Bislang galt das äußere Sonnensystem in der Wissenschaft als ein äußerst stabiles Konstrukt, bei dem selbst nach dem Tod der Sonne in einigen Milliarden Jahren die äußeren Planeten für weitere 30 bis 100 Milliarden Jahre geordnet auf ihren Bahnen verbleiben sollten. Zwar wird unsere Sonne als Roter Riese vermutlich die inneren Planeten zerstören, doch erst externe galaktische Einflüsse galten als endgültige Bedrohung für Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus und Neptun.
Ein Team von Forscher:innen um den Astronomen Konstantin Batygin am California Institute of Technology (Caltech) im US-amerikanischen Pasadena kommt nach neuen Analysen jedoch zu einem vollkommen anderen Ergebnis. Wie aus einer im Fachmagazin The Astrophysical Journal Letters veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, destabilisieren sich die Planetenbahnen vermutlich hundertmal schneller, als es bisherige Simulationen prognostiziert haben.
Ungleichmäßiger Masseverlust verändert die Bahnen

The threat is real, but still in the future, at least for now.
Anthropic's Frontier Red Team has demonstrated two components of a potential AI-powered worm that, if key issues with the practical implementation are resolved, could spread across consumer devices including inexpensive Android TV boxes and smart appliances, hypothetically without relying on datacenter infrastructure. The experiments show that AI agents can configure inference across different hardware platforms and orchestrate replication across a network. There are still some serious limitations, though, particularly around the gap between the capabilities of today's models versus the hardware constraints of potential targets.
In its October 12 report, titled "AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter," Anthropic examines a potential class of malware called a weight-based replicator. Rather than distributing conventional executable code, it would propagate AI model weights alongside the software infrastructure needed to run inference on compromised devices, and it's not pure theory, either.

articles.title: MIT startup says it can turn diesel trucks into cheaper hydrogen haulers — see it at Disrupt | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Diesel fuel powers everything from shipping to agriculture, and with prices hitting record highs in recent weeks, governments around the world are scrambling to contain the fallout.
For now, that’s meant releasing fuel from stockpiles, but in the coming years, the answer might be a new technology from an MIT startup called LNK Energies.
LNK has created a way to convert existing heavy-duty trucks from diesel to hydrogen, slashing pollution and costs while shielding operators from the price spikes that result from geopolitical instability like the war in Iran. “If you look at total cost of ownership of a Class 8 truck, it’s 13% cheaper than diesel,” Alexis Huynh, chief technology officer at LNK Energies, told TechCrunch. (Class 8 is the heaviest category of trucks, including big rigs.)
Automotive companies have been exploring the use of hydrogen in long-haul trucking in part because refilling a hydrogen tank is faster than recharging the massive batteries those trucks require. But hydrogen is challenging to move to refilling stations, and the pressure tanks required to store it on the truck are large and costly.
LNK’s approach is to carry hydrogen chemically attached to another compound. Liquid organic hydrogen carriers, or LOHCs, are liquids that can absorb and later release hydrogen, and they have been widely studied, but mostly for moving large quantities of hydrogen from refineries to fueling stations. The Backstage project has released version 1.55 of its open-source developer portal framework, adding automatic recovery for Software Template tasks that crash or time out. The release also removes a set of deprecated catalog APIs and moves the search module to Elasticsearch 8, so platform teams have several breaking changes to work through before they upgrade.
Task recovery sits behind a new scaffolder.taskRecovery configuration section. When it is enabled, the scaffolder resumes a task from the last completed step, keeps task secrets until the task reaches a terminal state and persists completed step outputs so later steps can read them. The release notes warn that actions used by recovered tasks should be idempotent or use checkpoints, because a resumed task can run an action a second time. The new section replaces three experimental flags, which still work as fallbacks.
The feature responds to a long-standing request. In April 2025, on a GitHub issue tracking scaffolder task retries, Manoj Azad wrote, "Currently, having to re-run the entire scaffolder process can be not only inconvenient but also problematic from a technical standpoint." The 1.55 feature covers tasks interrupted by a crash or time-out, which addresses part of that request.

Pero ¿qué ocurre cuando cada partida le cuesta dinero al estudio? Y no poco: la demo de 'Enseñar a conducir a mi hermana' está poniendo en jaque a sus desarrolladores.
Un simulador de conducción diferente. El juego parte de la premisa de la simulación, pero no encarnas al piloto, sino al pasajero. Quien conduce es tu hermana, de ahí el nombre. La gracia es que debes enseñarle a conducir a fuerza de explicárselo a viva voz.
En países como Estados Unidos, alguien sin carnet de conducir puede ponerse al volante si un copiloto experimentado hace de instructor, siempre que cuenten con permisos. Es justo el papel que recrea la demo de 'Enseñar a conducir a mi hermana' ('Teach my little sister how to drive'): empiezas diciéndole a tu hermana cómo arrancar el coche y terminas en contradirección sorteando coches de frente.

El juego utilizaba Google Gemini para interpretar lo que le dices a tu hermana y para las respuestas del propio juego, con ChatGPT como modelo secundario (el estudio actualmente prioriza a OpenAI). articles.title: Scheitern war keine Option: Warum ein OpenAI-Modell Chats fälschte und seine Testumgebung zerstörte

KI außer Kontrolle: OpenAI-Modell zerlegt grundlos seine eigene Umgebung
Ein OpenAI-Modell hat während der Absolvierung einer Testaufgabe absichtlich seine Untersuchungsumgebung zerstört. Der offensichtliche Grund: Der KI fehlten die Dateien, die es für seine Aufgabe gebraucht hätte. Nach mehreren Versuchen, die Ergebnisse zunächst zu fälschen, entschied es sich für die Zerlegung – offenbar in der Hoffnung, nach einem Neustart der Testumgebung an die fehlenden Dateien zu kommen. Den Vorfall beschreibt OpenAI in einem Blogpost. Das Modell war als „Bewerter“ in einen Reinforcement-Learning-Prozess eingebunden. Bei dieser Trainingsmethode lernt ein Modell durch Rückmeldungen, welche Antworten die korrekten sind. Das Bewerter-Modell sollte also Antworten aus anderen KI-Chats benoten. Doch die Dateien mit den gewünschten sieben Chats fehlten in seiner Testumgebung.
Erst erfundene Noten, dann erfundene Chats
Also gab die KI zunächst erfundene Bewertungen ab – offenbar, um aus der Rückmeldung des Prüfsystems abzulesen, welches Format die Ergebnisse haben müssen. Danach erstellte es sieben gefälschte Berichte, in denen es jeden Chat mit einer „4“ bewertete. Dass solche zufälligen Bewertungen unethisch sind, erkannte es laut seiner internen Dokumentation durchaus. Weil der Prüfprozess die Bewertungen nicht akzeptierte, dachte sich das Modell kurzerhand sieben Chats aus und verfasste dazu sieben passende Bewertungen. Doch auch das funktionierte nicht. Fritzbox als Werbeblocker: So verbannst du nervige Banner von deinem Smart-TV-Homescreen
Egal welcher Hersteller oder welches Betriebssystem: Mittlerweile spielen eigentlich alle Smart-TVs ab Werk Werbung direkt auf dem Homescreen ab. Für die Hersteller der Geräte ist das ein Milliardengeschäft. Nicht zuletzt, weil die Konsument:innen diese Anzeigen nicht einfach durch Werbeblocker unterbinden können, wie es etwa auf einem Desktop-Rechner möglich wäre.
Dabei gibt es durchaus technische Lösungen, um den Abruf von Werbeanzeigen im gesamten Heimnetzwerk zu unterbinden – und damit eben auch auf dem Smart-TV. Eine beliebte Lösung dafür ist die Software Pi-Hole. Die bietet euch eine Vielzahl an Optionen, um gezielt Verbindungen zu Werbe-Domains zu unterbinden. Allerdings hat das Ganze auch seine Nachteile.
Ihr benötigt einen Raspberry Pi oder einen anderen Computer, der permanent aktiviert sein muss, damit Pi-Hole funktioniert. Außerdem solltet ihr zumindest über rudimentäre Linux- oder Docker-Kenntnisse verfügen, um die Software installieren zu können.
Besitzer einer Fritzbox können auf ein so kompliziertes Setup zukünftig allerdings verzichten. Denn ab Fritz OS 8.40 beziehungsweise 8.50 könnt ihr direkt auf den Routern des deutschen Herstellers Filterlisten hinterlegen, mit denen auch der Abruf von Werbeanzeigen durch euren Smart-TV unterbunden werden kann.

The rise of private spacetech in India is frequently celebrated through triumphant headlines, but behind every successful rocket launch or satellite deployment lies a gritty reality defined by hundreds of investor rejections, acute supply chain bottlenecks, and the constant threat of orbital failure.
Speaking with Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO, YourStory and The Bharat Project, at the 17th edition of YourStory’s flagship tech-startup event, TechSparks, Srinath Ravichandran, Co-founder and CEO of AgniKul Cosmos, and Suyash Singh, Co-founder and CEO of GalaxEye, shared practical insights into the complex task of building aerospace ventures in an emerging market.
When AgniKul started in 2017, the Indian regulatory framework for private space technology was still evolving, and local venture capital for deeptech was nearly non-existent. Ravichandran faced 275 investor rejections before securing initial backing. Singh encountered similar headwinds at GalaxEye, facing roughly 100 rejections. Their early survival required breaking down ambitious goals into manageable steps rather than relying on rigid long-term master plans.

articles.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation makes a strong first impression
articles.summary:
For me, the most powerful narrative beat in Final Fantasy VII isn’t actually Aerith’s tragic death scene. While that undoubtedly hits hard, what’s always resonated with me far more strongly is Cloud’s journey towards overcoming his trauma and deep-seated insecurities and ultimately discovering himself with the help of childhood friend Tifa. That arc has meant so much to me over the years, and it’s the single most important thing that I’ve been hoping Square Enix’s bold Final Fantasy VII Remake project will deliver on.
Based on my recent hands-on time with the final instalment in the trilogy, Final Fantasy VII Revelation, I’m feeling even more confident that director Naoki Hamaguchi and co. will stick the landing. Admittedly, I was conflicted on how 2024’s Rebirth handled Aerith’s fate, as murky and bombastic as that climax proved to be. But something both Rebirth and Remake have done beautifully is dramatically expand upon the exploration of Cloud’s ever-worsening fragile mental state, and my Revelation demo showed how Square Enix is continuing to push that forward.

If there’s one lesson the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident taught us, it’s that AI agents can be unpredictable.
“Imagine if something like that happened in the physical world,” Howie Sun, CEO and co-founder of Laplace Intelligence, told TechCrunch. “AI agents are moving from computers into the real world, and we don’t really want physical AI to fail in the real world.”
Ann Arbor-based Laplace is building automated red-teaming — essentially, stress-testing a system by deliberately trying to make it fail — for robotics and physical AI. The company is betting that the only way to make sure physical AI is safe is to have AI test it.
“Our goal is to help companies discover and fix problems before deployment — and, over time, build a shared foundation of evidence that customers, insurers, and regulators can trust,” Sun said.
Laplace is one of 20 startups competing in Startup Battlefield 200, the startup pitch competition taking place at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco this week, October 13-15. It will present on the Disrupt Stage Tuesday afternoon, October 13.
Sun, alongside his co-founder and chief scientist Henry Liu, founded Laplace a year ago out of the University of Michigan. Sun has spent the last eight years in academia researching how to challenge autonomous driving AI in simulation. Sin embargo, advirtió que los avances actuales acercan un escenario en el que una IA podría pasar de un aparato a otro, instalarse en equipos vulnerables y utilizar su capacidad de procesamiento de forma distribuida.
La empresa detrás de Claude señaló que el riesgo no es inmediato porque los modelos pequeños aún no combinan suficiente capacidad con un tamaño adecuado para funcionar en muchos dispositivos limitados.

articles.title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse is a successful resurrection, but not without faults
articles.summary:
This year has been quite the story for dormant platformer franchises, especially Castlevania.
It’s been nearly 20 years since we’ve had a single-player Metroidvania-style Castlevania game. My introduction to the franchise was with Symphony of the Night over a decade ago, and since then, I was hooked. It’s a prime example of a sublime platformer game, with perfect controls, interesting world-building and a rich atmosphere.
Since then, I’ve played through the various Castlevania games led by Koji Igarashi, who spearheaded the Metroidvania titles, including his spiritual successor, Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night. Despite the lack of Castlevania video game releases, though, the franchise itself was still active through various other media, including the fantastic Netflix TV series and video game collaborations.
The most famous of these collaborations was with Dead Cells, a roguelite (where players get randomized gear during each run) game inspired by the Metroidvania genre. After rave reviews (though I personally haven’t played it), it felt fitting for Konami to give Castlevania the “Sonic Mania” treatment with the creators of Dead Cells taking the helm for the newest iteration, Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse.
How does it compare to its previous iterations or even the endless Metroidvania games out there now? Well, it has its highs and lows that will ultimately determine whether you really jive with it.

articles.title: Forget rockets — Longshot wants to fire cargo into space from a gun. See it at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Rockets are, infamously, a real pain in the butt. Our old friend physics forces rockets to be built with almost no room for error, and even then only a small fraction of their weight makes it to orbit.
There are, at least in theory, other ways to do the job — space elevators, centrifuges, or a big chain hanging from a satellite in space and scooping up cargo from Earth. (Blue Origin spent some time thinking about that one before the idea wound up in a Neal Stephenson novel.)
And then there’s an idea dating all the way back to Jules Verne: Use a big gun to shoot a projectile into space.
Longshot Space Technology, a startup based in Alameda, California, is working on exactly that. The co-founders, CEO Mike Grace and CTO Nato Saichek, see an opportunity to take a technology that has already proven its worth and apply it to the pressing need for space launch. The startup has raised about $20 million from venture investors in service of its mission.
When it comes to frontier technology, Grace says, “you can build something that has a lot of novelty, or you can do something really hard. You don’t get to do both.” He points to SpaceX as an example of a company that has “taken classically de-risked technology and scaled it aggressively.” What SpaceX did with NASA rocket research, he says, Longshot will do with multi-injection guns — designs that give a projectile extra boosts as it moves down the barrel — built for World War II and during 1960s research programs.

articles.title: Die trügerische Sicherheit offener KI: Wie in Open-Weight-Modellen Schadcode versteckt wird
articles.summary:
Trügerische Transparenz: Die Sicherheitslücke in Open-Weight-Modellen
Die Bereitstellung sogenannter Open-Weight-Modelle ist in der Softwareentwicklung etabliert. Im Gegensatz zu Closed-Source-Ansätzen gewähren die Herausgeber hierbei den Zugriff auf die fertig trainierten Parameter, die sogenannten Gewichte, des neuronalen Netzes.
Das vermittelt Anwender:innen den Eindruck, die Architektur nachvollziehen und auf Sicherheitsrisiken prüfen zu können. Ein Team von Wissenschaftlern um Andis Draguns vom Forschungsinstitut Contramont Research aus dem kalifornischen San Francisco und der britischen Universität Oxford belegt, dass diese Annahme fehlerhaft ist.
Kryptografische Schließfächer in Open-Weight-Modellen
Wie in einer auf dem Preprint-Server Arxiv veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, haben die Forscher eine Methode entwickelt, um Fähigkeiten in den Gewichten von KI-Modellen zu verstecken. Sie nutzen das Konzept der sogenannten Digital Lockers, bei dem Daten kryptografisch versiegelt werden.
Die Wissenschaftler verschlüsseln ein ausführbares Sub-Netzwerk und betten es in ein größeres Trägermodell ein. Dafür nutzen sie die Hash-Funktion Keccak, die unter anderem die Basis für den aktuellen Verschlüsselungsstandard SHA-3 bildet.

Reading about all that damage, to both infrastructure and animals, inspired Sara Nozkova (pictured above on the left) to develop a wildlife-deterrent system that works differently from the sirens, lights, fences, falcons, and culling traditionally used to keep animals away from roads, train tracks, airports, and other infrastructure.

Microsoft pidió a usuarios y administradores de sistemas que preparen sus equipos para una renovación de los certificados digitales utilizados por Windows Update. Si algunos dispositivos no reciben los parches necesarios antes de las fechas límite de 2027, podrían perder la conexión con el servicio y dejar de recibir futuras actualizaciones de seguridad. El aviso abarca distintas versiones de Windows 11 y Windows Server.
El problema no se debe a una nueva vulnerabilidad ni significa que los equipos hayan sido atacados. Los certificados digitales sirven para verificar la conexión segura entre los dispositivos y los servicios de actualización. Como tienen una fecha de vencimiento, deben renovarse para que Windows Update pueda seguir funcionando correctamente.
Los plazos varían según el sistema operativo. Para la mayoría de los dispositivos afectados, la fecha clave será el 19 de junio de 2027. Sin embargo, algunos equipos empresariales deberán estar preparados antes, el 17 de mayo de ese año.
Qué equipos deben instalar los parches
Los dispositivos con Windows 11 24H2 y Windows Server 2025 deberán tener instalada la actualización de seguridad de septiembre de 2025 o una posterior antes del 19 de junio de 2027. El mismo plazo se aplica a otras versiones compatibles de Windows 11, Windows Server 2022 y las ediciones de Windows 10 que todavía reciben soporte, aunque para estos sistemas Microsoft establece como requisito la actualización de seguridad de julio de 2026 o una posterior…

Pero entre los menos exóticos, hay uno que se repite con cierta asiduidad: ¿puedo meter dos vehículos en mi plaza de garaje?
Dos (o tres o cuatro o cinco) vehículos por el precio de uno. Un garaje comunitario es ese espacio dividido en pequeñas parcelas privadas con entrada, salida y un paso común para el movimiento de los vehículos. Por defecto, podríamos pensar que si el aparcamiento tiene 100 plazas, el número de vehículos que puedan cobijarse bajo techo será otro centenar.
Las dudas surgen cuando un vecino utiliza esa misma plaza para guardar dos vehículos. Un coche y una moto suele ser lo más habitual pero pensemos, por ejemplo, en un coche y una o más bicicletas o, sencillamente, en cuatro o cinco motos. Y ahí empiezan los conflictos.

articles.title: Niobia takes the guesswork out of some of tech's most expensive mistakes | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
San Francisco-based startup Niobia is betting big on a critical but often overlooked part of battery and chip making: helping engineers understand how and why things go wrong. Its AI software flags production defects and lets engineers ask a chatbot what caused them, aiming to deliver answers in minutes rather than days.
How it works (broadly): The company’s customers place AI agents on their production lines to look for defects, then loop in human engineers to work out what might cause a product to fail. The agents run on self-contained GPUs mounted directly on manufacturing equipment, much like a sensor. They can spot pinhole-sized flaws such as scratches. Niobia’s AI also gathers all the data in one place so engineers can ask a chatbot what went wrong and dig deeper into the cause.
Speed is so critical because chips and batteries are some of the world’s most important products, while also increasingly in short supply. As manufacturers continue to develop and improve their technologies, things inevitably go awry during research and development. Engineers then spend days or longer figuring out a fix before they can restart production. Each flaw or mistake can prove costly — sometimes running into the millions of dollars — and set back manufacturing timelines.

articles.title: En España cada vez hay más gente haciendo 200 kilómetros en coche todos los días para ir a trabajar
articles.summary:
Vivir a 110 kilómetros del trabajo parece una forma de ahorrar, pero lo que se ahorra en alquiler se paga en coche, en tiempo y en sueño. Aunque hay quien prefiere conducir, como María Inmaculada Jiménez, quien lleva la gerencia de un restaurante en La Cala de Mijas (Málaga), pero vive en Mollina, en el interior de la provincia. Según contaba El Mundo, recorre 220 kilómetros diarios entre ida y vuelta para poder pagar una casa que en la costa no podría permitirse.
Es un caso extremo pero no aislado que en inglés denominan super-commuting. El problema es el de siempre: que la tecnología te permite vivir lejos del trabajo no significa nada en sí mismo. Porque la argolla sigue siendo la misma: salario insuficiente para pagar una casa.
A todos lados con portátil. Un estudio de Stanford sobre dos millones de trayectos en las diez mayores ciudades de EEUU detectó que los desplazamientos de 40 millas (unos 64 km) o más han pasado del 15,8% al 18,5% del total desde la pandemia. Los supercommutes de 75 millas (unos 120 km) o más han crecido casi un tercio hasta rondar el 3% de los trayectos, y suelen costar unas dos horas y veinte por sentido.
Quien no tiene que ir a la oficina cada día tolera un trayecto largo una o dos veces por semana si a cambio gana espacio y nivel de vida, claro. Según estos estudios, los más jóvenes y quienes tienen ingresos altos son quienes viven más lejos. Broadcom executives said the product responds to attacks that are accelerating faster than enterprises can update infrastructure software.

HyperArmor operates directly at the ESX layer, which runs directly on a physical server to support virtual machines. Protecting the hypervisor is important because it undergirds all workloads that depend on that host.

XMEMS starts mass-producing chips that cool AI glasses, smartphones and data centers
Silicon chip startup xMEMS Labs Inc. today said it has started mass production of its XMC-2400 and XMC-4800 chips for cooling artificial intelligence hardware.
No one has commercialized solid-state active cooling at this scale before, according to the company.
The chips are aimed at AI hardware running into heat limits in two places. Conventional fans “simply cannot fit” in AI glasses and smartphones that still need active heat removal, said Mike Housholder, vice president and general manager of the thermal management business unit at xMEMS. For data centers, the company is targeting solid-state drives, laser modules and other parts left outside the liquid cooling that increasingly surrounds high-power processors.
The technology behind both chips came out of the company’s speaker business, where an electrical signal flexes a thin silicon membrane to produce sound. In the cooling chips, the same type of membrane moves air. Device makers can route the air down narrow channels to a processor or a memory chip, the company said, since it builds high pressure.
Nothing in the package spins. Because each device is a single piece of silicon, Housholder said, it could eventually be packaged together with the AI processors it cools.
Personal SSDs and glasses built for AI or extended reality are the target for the XMC-2400. The XMC-4800 moves more air, enough for thermally demanding AI smartphones as wel…

articles.title: Llevamos años cambiando las sábanas cada semana. La ciencia apunta a que lo importante no es cuándo las cambias, sino cómo las lavas
articles.summary:
Dentro de los hogares hay diferentes debates en torno a con qué frecuencia hacer diferentes tareas, como por ejemplo el cambio de sábanas de nuestras camas. Aquí hay familias donde las sábanas se cambian cada semana, en otras cada dos y otras personas que se olvidan completamente de esto. Pero aquí los expertos apuntan a que lo importante está sobre todo en la temperatura de lavado.
El origen de los siete días. Aunque es un consejo que se ha transmitido entre las diferentes generaciones de una familia, la realidad es que la cifra de los 7 a 10 días no sale de ningún ensayo clínico. Aquí debemos entender que este rango de fechas responde a una pauta de control específica para las personas alérgicas a los ácaros del polvo. Y está avalado por las instituciones sanitarias.
Además, tenemos como referencia un estudio clásico de Vyszenski-Moher publicado en 2002 que demostró que las especies comunes de ácaros no necesitan un cambio de sábanas cada semana, sino que hace falta una temperatura alta para romper su ciclo vital. Es por ello que estamos ante un mito temporal, puesto que no existe ningún estudio primario que demuestre que cambiar las sábanas cada 7 días frente a cada 14 tenga un impacto real en la salud de la población general.
La verdadera clave. Aunque estamos obsesionados con seguir una rutina concreta, la clave está en la temperatura del agua con la que lavamos las sábanas. Y aquí un estudio publicado en 2008 nos descubrió lo que pasaba con los ácaros a diferentes tempe…

articles.title: Spranic builds spatial memory for physical AI - SiliconANGLE

Spranic builds spatial memory for physical AI
Physical AI needs context about its surroundings to adapt beyond a fixed set of instructions.
Munich-based Spranic is building a spatial memory layer that records physical spaces and how they change. Connecting that information with knowledge graphs could help robots interpret their environments across different tasks, according to Jordi Spranger (pictured), founder and chief executive officer of Spranic.
“Robots deserve the right context at the right time across domains,” he said. “This is the problem we’re tackling. We can see that this works really well for digital agents already. Now we’re bringing this to the physical world.”
Spranger spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier for theCUBE + NYSE Wired: AI Luminaries interview series on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how knowledge graphs could help robots adapt tasks and make their decisions auditable. (* Disclosure below.)
Giving physical AI reusable context
Adapting machines to changing environments remains a challenge for physical AI. Reusable spatial context can reduce the task-specific planning required for robot deployments, according to Spranger.
“But for robots, maps are a really big part,” he said. [Robots] need Google Maps on steroids to be really free from a statically planned task [so they] can replan across a lot of tasks that a humanoid could do.”

Los números del estudio clínico

La compañía, conocida por Fortnite, Unreal Engine y su tienda digital, buscaría situar la IA generativa en el centro de su proceso de desarrollo, aunque conservaría la supervisión de equipos humanos.
La información cobra relevancia porque plantea un cambio en la producción de juegos comerciales de alto presupuesto. Epic ya ha incorporado herramientas de inteligencia artificial en Unreal Engine y en personajes de Fortnite, pero el supuesto título de Disney llevaría esa estrategia a un producto basado en franquicias como Marvel y Star Wars.
Epic Games prepararía un cambio en la producción de videojuegos
Según la información atribuida a fuentes internas, Epic Games avanzaría hacia un flujo de trabajo centrado en inteligencia artificial. El objetivo sería utilizar sistemas generativos para acelerar tareas de programación, creación artística y diseño de recursos dentro de los videojuegos.
El cambio no significaría que los desarrolladores desaparezcan del proceso. Los equipos humanos mantendrían la responsabilidad de revisar el contenido generado, corregir errores y decidir qué elementos cumplen con los estándares técnicos y creativos necesarios para llegar a una versión final.

Les prix à la pompe en 2026 frappent aussi de plein fouet les auto-écoles, désormais prêtes à répercuter ces frais supplémentaires sur le prix du permis de conduire.
Alimentée par les tensions au Moyen-Orient, l’explosion des prix du carburant impacte de nombreuses professions, dont les auto-écoles. Avec des flottes automobiles qui parcourent souvent entre 45 000 et 60 000 km par véhicule chaque année, l’augmentation du prix du litre pèse lourd dans les comptes. Face à cette situation, de nombreux gérants n’ont d’autre choix que de répercuter cette hausse directement sur le coût de la formation au permis de conduire.
Une facture qui s’alourdit pour les futurs conducteurs
Selon plusieurs gérants interrogés par l’AFP, les dépenses en carburant auraient progressé de 30 à 40 % depuis le début de la crise. Une situation qui pousse logiquement certaines auto-écoles à ajuster leurs tarifs. À Rennes, un établissement a été contraint d’augmenter son taux horaire de 52 à 55 €, ajoutant près de 90 € sur un forfait classique de trente heures.
À l’échelle nationale, l’ECF (École de conduite française) estime que la hausse pourrait atteindre 150 à 200 € sur un forfait actuellement facturé autour de 1 600 €, soit une augmentation de 9 à 12,5 %. Un obstacle supplémentaire pour les jeunes candidats, alors que le permis représente déjà un budget conséquent.

GTA 6 Reportedly Coming to PC in Q1 2027
Rockstar is planning to bring GTA 6 to PC sometime in the first quarter of 2027, according to a new report from GamesBeat. The outlet cites four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans, all of whom asked to stay anonymous. If accurate, PC players would get the game between January and March 2027, just a few months after its November 19 launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar still hasn't announced a PC version, and PC was left out of the launch plans from the start. Interestingly, if the timing pans out, that would be a much shorter wait than last time. GTA 5 hit consoles in September 2013 and only reached PC in April 2015, roughly 19 months later. 
This could matter for the roleplay ecosystem too, since FiveM, the framework behind most GTA 5 roleplay servers, runs only on PC, and GTA 6's online mode is already tipped for 2027. Of course, early PC launch windows have surfaced before that haven't exactly panned out. A Corsair executive floated an early 2026 launch last year, a comment Corsair later called speculation, and VGC's Andy Robinson suggested last month that the PC version might show up sooner than people expect. A Q1 2027 release would also arrive before Take-Two's fiscal year closes on March 31, 2027. Until Rockstar says something, readers are advised to treat this as a well-sourced rumor and not a confirmed date.

La cyberattaque choquante contre les frigos des supermarchés français n'est pas la seule attaque inquiétante. Car le même jour aux Pays-Bas, un autre géant de la distribution a été attaqué.
Est-on sûr de la viabilité de nos grandes infrastructures en cas de crise ? VPN dark web alerts vs. free tools: Are you paying extra for repackaged data?
VPN providers are increasingly selling “dark web alerts” as premium security features, marketing them as essential protection against identity theft. This raises a key question: do paid alerts find unique threats, or just repackage data that's freely available?
With subscriptions to the best VPNs already costing up to $10-15 monthly, adding identity protection features can push bills toward $20 a month. If you’re essentially paying for data available at no cost, that’s money better spent elsewhere.
This article is the third in a series of content relating to Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2026, which runs throughout October. The previous articles have covered VPN protection when using AI, and the benefits of dedicated antivirus over packaged solutions.
How dark web monitoring works
Let’s clear up a common misconception first: VPN services aren’t sending security analysts to actively patrol the dark web hunting for your name. That would be impossible – the dark web is too vast and constantly shifting.
Instead, what most dark web monitoring services actually do is simpler: they cross-reference your information against massive databases of leaked credentials that have already been publicly disclosed. These databases contain billions of compromised accounts from data breaches spanning over a decade.

Publiée le 12 octobre 2026 dans la revue Nature Cities, une étude pilotée par Shengli Tao et Xie Hu, chercheurs à l'université de Pékin, a mesuré entre 2014 et 2023 les mouvements verticaux du sol dans 465 villes de plus d'un million d'habitants, réparties sur 107 pays. articles.title: Low-Cost Android Phones Ship With Preinstalled Malware That Turns Them Into Residential Proxies

Low-cost Android smartphones have been shipped with malicious software baked into the device firmware, allowing bad actors to covertly install apps, conduct ad fraud, and turn devices into residential proxies.
The activity, which targets Android devices built on MediaTek platforms across several brands, is being tracked by Bitdefender under the moniker Midnight Mimosa.
The preinstalled malware ("com.android.system.lite") runs with system-level privileges, which make it possible to install or uninstall a rotating set of at least 32 disguised apps, grant itself additional permissions to accessibility services, notifications, and SMS, and load arbitrary code supplied remotely by the operators.
Specifically, it fetches a remote configuration from an external server and then downloads and executes additional payloads designed to conduct ad fraud and silent installation or removal of partner apps. These apps incorporate proxyware, ad fraud, and code execution features. It can also grant permission to any Android app package.
"This essentially means its operators could install and delete apps at will, tuning each device to their needs, including making them part of large botnets," the Romanian cybersecurity company said.
"This scheme is likely designed mainly to generate revenue. The operators carry out ad and click fraud, collect device and installed-app information, and turn infected devices into residential-proxy relay nodes, making them zombies in botnets."

articles.title: Attackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges Up to 50°C by Hijacking Danfoss Controllers
articles.summary:
Attackers took remote control of fridges and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets on the night of October 11 and warmed them, forcing stores to throw food away, several retail chains said.
The attackers reached them through the controller that runs all of a store's fridges and freezers, a device made by Danish company Danfoss that maintenance firms can manage remotely. Les Mousquetaires, which owns the Intermarché chain, said its fridges and freezers were put into defrost and heated to as much as 50°C.
CERT-FR, the French government's computer emergency response team, said in an alert published in French on October 12 that it is aware of numerous compromises affecting two Danfoss controller series, the AK-SM and the AK-SC. It told operators to disconnect the controllers or filter access to them.
CERT-FR is part of ANSSI, France's national cybersecurity agency. ANSSI's head, Vincent Strubel, called it urgent to take the two series off the internet or filter access very tightly, AFP reported.
Neither French authorities nor Danfoss has so far said who carried out the attack or how the attackers got into the controllers. Danfoss said most of the units hit were older models that it no longer updates.
Which Chains Were Hit
The chains gave their own figures to AFP, Reuters and broadcaster RTL. Each counts the stores the attack reached.

articles.summary:
Three vulnerabilities in LG's webOS can be chained to give an attacker on the same local network root access to certain smart TVs without a PIN or any interaction from the owner.
LG has issued a fix, according to an advisory published by SSD Secure Disclosure on October 12.
The chain was tested on two TV models, the 32LQ636BPSA and the 27TQ600SW, running webOS 7.5.7-25 on firmware 04.54.40. Whether other models or firmware versions are affected is not known.
Owners of affected TVs should check for a firmware update. No workaround is available for those who cannot update yet.
The attack enters through a service that the TV exposes on port 3001, which is used by the LG ThinQ app for pairing. An attacker replays a manifest from sync-demo, a built-in app already on the device, signed with a test certificate the firmware trusts. A permission in the manifest causes the pairing service to skip the PIN prompt and hand over a privileged key.
With that key, the attacker launches another built-in app, cmp-client, and points it to an attacker-controlled page. The app does not check where it navigates, and the loaded page keeps access to PalmServiceBridge, an internal interface to the TV's system services.
Through that bridge, the attacker calls the system logging service, pmlogd, passing shell commands through an input field the service does not check. Because pmlogd runs as root, the injected command runs as root.

With AI accelerating reconnaissance, exploitation of vulnerabilities, and privilege escalation, attackers can move through systems faster than security teams can investigate. A compromised account that looks legitimate at first could become the starting point for a much larger attack.
And that's where traditional identity security faces a serious problem: Checking who gets access isn't enough if you can't control what happens after.
Why Traditional Identity Controls Are Falling Behind
Many identity security controls focus on authentication, permissions, and access policies. But what happens when a trusted identity is compromised, its behavior changes, or an attacker begins exploiting already granted privileges?
That gap becomes more dangerous as AI-powered attacks accelerate.
Attackers can automate parts of the attack chain while defenders are still collecting alerts, investigating activity, and deciding how to respond.
The answer isn't simply detecting attacks faster. It's the ability to evaluate and control access in real time while an identity is actively being used.
This is the idea behind runtime identity security.

Anthropic warns these AI worms could use multiple compromised IoT devices to run inference while carrying its model weights with it as it reproduces. IoT devices would be a prime target for this worm because they are “cheap and typically poorly defended,” the company says.

GitHub has taken the step of expiring unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations 48 hours after creation after researchers found that it was possible for an attacker to push new versions of a different user's package without having to steal their credentials.

The development comes in response to findings from Bloom Security, which discovered a loophole within npm's trusted publishing to take over thousands of packages and trigger a Shai-Hulud-style cascading supply chain attack. The findings were reported to GitHub on June 6, 2026.

articles.title: SAP Discloses Critical CVSS 10 Flaw in Cloud SDK for Python Allowing OAuth2 Credential Theft
articles.summary:
A flaw in SAP's Cloud SDK for Python can send an application's OAuth2 client credentials to a server an attacker controls, SAP said in a security advisory on October 13. The flaw affects multi-tenant applications on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) that use the SDK, SAP's official Python client for BTP services. An attacker must be able to control the tenant subdomain, the name such an application passes to the SDK to say which tenant a request is for.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-89111 and carries SAP's CVSS score of 10.0 out of 10. The advisory names version 0.45.2, released on August 21, as the fix.
The SDK handles authentication for those services with the application's client credentials, a client ID and a client secret. Version 0.45.2 added a check that rejects any tenant subdomain that is not a simple name.
Six later releases do not apply that check in every case, The Hacker News found. Versions 0.53.0 through 0.55.0, published between September 10 and September 18, skip it when an application calls the SDK's Destination service module.
Version 0.53.0 moved that module onto new shared code for requesting tokens, and that code did not include the check. Version 0.55.1 added it there on September 18.
Passing a tenant subdomain that contains URL delimiters "now raises ValueError immediately instead of silently routing credentials to an attacker-controlled endpoint," the 0.55.1 release notes say.

articles.title: Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another
articles.summary:
A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it.
The flaw was in the feature that converts a personal account into an organization, Docker said in a security advisory on October 12. Conversion transferred the account's personal access tokens (PATs) to the user designated as the organization's owner. A PAT is used in place of a password in the registry, and the person who created each token can still use it.
The access was limited to the registry. It did not reach the Docker Hub web interface, and it could not be used to change a password, email address, or two-factor settings, or to take over an account.
Docker tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-105445 and rated it critical. The CVE record it published on October 13 gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.4.
The flaw was open from August 26, 2024, until the fix, a little over two years. Docker made the fix on Docker Hub itself, so there is no update to install.
Docker Hub cannot move a repository from one account to another. A user instead converts a personal account into an organization that keeps the same name, and must name an existing account as its owner.

articles.title: Anthropic Warns Small AI Models Could Soon Form Self-Propagating IoT Botnets
articles.summary:
Small artificial intelligence (AI) models may be months away from developing capabilities to self-replicate on IoT devices like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes, according to a warning from Anthropic.
The frontier AI lab said small AI models could form autonomous, self-propagating worm botnets that are "challenging to shut down," since "there's no centralized point to shut off."
Prior work has demonstrated that AI agents can act like one by scanning their network, executing an exploit, and copying model weights to a target machine across a GPU cluster with an aim to generate tailored attack strategies and use compromised machines as a botnet to run large language models (LLMs) in order to sustain its reasoning and expand in scale.
"Such an 'AI worm' could carry its model weights with it as it reproduces (or re-download them from a public hub), and then run inference directly on compromised hardware," Anthropic said. "Effectively, the weights would become part of the malware payload."
The idea, at a high level, explains how AI models could potentially break into internet-connected devices and use their computing power to run themselves and spread to other devices, without having to rely on expensive data centers all the time. A more powerful model that's too large to fit into a single device could be split into small chunks and run across multiple machines to collectively run it.
